about: Answer choices for the Question Bank's written-answer questions; written by scripts/question_choices.py.

options: From our conscience, personal experience, and the guidance of human reason
From pastors and church leadership who receive God's direct revelation to the church
From church tradition and the consensus of Christian teachers throughout history
From the Bible, through which God revealed Himself as the supreme standard for belief and living
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: From the Bible, through which God revealed Himself as the supreme standard for belief and living

options: His body was restored to normal human form and remained on earth
He appeared only as a vision or phantom to His disciples
Raised from the dead with a glorified body and appeared to disciples
His spirit rose to heaven but His body remained in the tomb
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Raised from the dead with a glorified body and appeared to disciples

options: Jesus stayed on earth in His disciples and remains invisible
Jesus ascended into heaven and is now exalted to honor and power
Jesus returned to heaven but remains distant and uninvolved with the world
Jesus is seated at God's right hand but has no power
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Jesus ascended into heaven and is now exalted to honor and power

options: He will return in power and glory to judge the world.
He will come to earth as a humble servant to teach again
He will return invisibly but will not judge anyone
He has already returned in the form of the Holy Spirit
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: He will return in power and glory to judge the world.

options: The Holy Spirit is God's power but not a person or divine being
The Holy Spirit is less divine than God the Father and Son
The Holy Spirit is a created being sent by God to help us
The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of God and is fully divine.
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of God and is fully divine.

options: He sanctified the church, comforted believers in sorrow, and gave them spiritual gifts
He prepared John the Baptist, convicted sinners of sin, and worked only through prophets
He guided the priesthood, revealed God's law at Sinai, and dwelt in the temple
He was involved in creation, inspired holy men to write Scripture, empowered Jesus, and raised Him
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: He was involved in creation, inspired holy men to write Scripture, empowered Jesus, and raised Him

options: Evolved from animals and differ only in degree, not essential nature
Made in God's image but destined to achieve God-like power
In God's image, male and female, with purpose to know and enjoy God
Created as servants of God with no significance or special value
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: In God's image, male and female, with purpose to know and enjoy God

options: God created man both innocent and with a natural inclination to sin
Man was created with knowledge of good and evil and ability to choose
Created innocent with free choice, man sinned, bringing sin and death
God predestined man to sin so that Christ could provide salvation
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Created innocent with free choice, man sinned, bringing sin and death

options: Satan's temptation affected only Adam and Eve, not all people
Man fell through Satan's temptation, so all are born inclined to sin
People sin because they live in a sinful environment, not by nature
Satan caused all humans to sin immediately upon their birth
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Man fell through Satan's temptation, so all are born inclined to sin

options: Sin is only when we intentionally break rules we know about
Only actions that harm others or break human laws constitute sin
Contrary to God's will or not done as faith for God's glory
Thoughts and feelings are not sinful; only deliberate actions are
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Contrary to God's will or not done as faith for God's glory

options: Only redeemed people are truly valued by God; unbelievers have lesser worth
God values people according to their good works and moral accomplishments in life
Human life becomes sacred only after baptism and personal profession of Christian faith
Every human being is greatly valued by God; God created us in His image and Christ died for us
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Every human being is greatly valued by God; God created us in His image and Christ died for us

options: Church councils selected and approved writings that became the Bible we have today
Men inspired by God wrote the Bible, making God its author, without error and totally true
Different men wrote the Bible over centuries with some mistakes but mostly truth
Prophets and apostles wrote the Bible with guidance from church leaders
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Men inspired by God wrote the Bible, making God its author, without error and totally true

options: Yes, we must earn God's love through perfect obedience
God's love only comes to those who truly believe in Him
We must first earn God's love through obedience and good works
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: No! God loved us first.

options: God's holiness hates sin, His justice punishes it, separating us under condemnation
God tolerates sin if we confess it and promise to improve
God's punishment for sin is harsh, but His love prevents Him from enforcing it
Sin harms us but God overlooks it because of His mercy
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God's holiness hates sin, His justice punishes it, separating us under condemnation

options: Salvation is through baptism and faith in Jesus Christ as Lord
Salvation comes through faith in Christ combined with good works and obedience
Salvation requires faith in Christ plus keeping God's commandments perfectly
Salvation is only through grace of God and personal faith in Jesus Christ
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Salvation is only through grace of God and personal faith in Jesus Christ

options: God's foreknowledge of who would freely choose to believe in Jesus Christ
God's calling of believers to grow in grace and spiritual maturity after conversion
God's plan to save those who persevere in faith and obedience to His law
God's eternal plan, formed before the world began, to save sinners through spreading the Gospel
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God's eternal plan, formed before the world began, to save sinners through spreading the Gospel

options: People must first repent of their sins before God begins to work in them
Sincere people who truly desire God are naturally and gradually drawn to Him
God must first work in their hearts to attract them, because people are sinful and unwilling for God's rule
God makes salvation possible, but people must make the final decision to accept
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God must first work in their hearts to attract them, because people are sinful and unwilling for God's rule

options: He enables understanding of truth, makes them appreciate Jesus's goodness, convicts of sin and judgment, and calls as Savior
He shows the law, brings conviction, and works only through the preaching of the word
He works exclusively through Christian witness and example, not directly in the human heart
He enables moral improvement, guides their conscience, and creates saving faith gradually
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: He enables understanding of truth, makes them appreciate Jesus's goodness, convicts of sin and judgment, and calls as Savior

options: In repentance toward God and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ
In confession of sins to a priest and sincere regret
In a public declaration of faith before witnesses
In baptism and joining a local Christian church
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: In repentance toward God and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ

options: Repentance is a sincere change of mind and of attitude in which the sinner turns to God from sin
Repentance is admitting guilt before God and asking His forgiveness and restoration
Repentance is turning from sin and performing good works to make proper restitution
Repentance is feeling deeply sorry for sin and making a commitment to change behavior
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Repentance is a sincere change of mind and of attitude in which the sinner turns to God from sin

options: Believing the right facts about Jesus and understanding the gospel message correctly
Trusting Jesus to forgive you, change your life, and provide you a home in Heaven
Having faith that God exists and trusting he will help you in trouble
Knowing about Jesus and committing to follow his teachings and obey his laws
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Trusting Jesus to forgive you, change your life, and provide you a home in Heaven

options: Sanctification; the lifelong work of the Spirit empowering believers to overcome sinful nature
Baptism; being initiated into the church and publicly committing to Christian community
New life; being born again; the Holy Spirit makes people alive to God and changes their direction
Conversion; making a mental agreement with Christian truth and a commitment to Christ
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: New life; being born again; the Holy Spirit makes people alive to God and changes their direction

options: One of many spiritual beings who rules over the universe
A distant, unknown power that created the world and withdrew
An impersonal force that guides the universe and all creation
The only living and true God, first and best of all beings
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The only living and true God, first and best of all beings

options: When a person becomes Christian, God makes them part of His eternal family as children of God
All people are God's children equally through creation; adoption adds special privilege
Adoption happens only after years of faithful service and demonstration of spiritual maturity
Only church members who keep covenant with God are adopted into His eternal family
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: When a person becomes Christian, God makes them part of His eternal family as children of God

options: Being set apart for God and growing toward spiritual maturity through the Holy Spirit
Becoming free from all sin and living a perfect life that pleases God
Growing in faith and knowledge by studying the Bible and obeying all laws
A process of removing evil desires and becoming completely holy through discipline
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Being set apart for God and growing toward spiritual maturity through the Holy Spirit

options: The Holy Spirit gives believers special abilities and spiritual gifts for God's service
The Holy Spirit fills believers at Pentecost to empower them for witnessing
At salvation the Holy Spirit baptizes believers into Christ's Body and comes to live inside them
After water baptism the Holy Spirit comes to dwell within the believer permanently
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: At salvation the Holy Spirit baptizes believers into Christ's Body and comes to live inside them

options: He guides morality, strengthens faith through trials, gives wisdom, and intercedes in prayer
He assures salvation, empowers character development, helps in prayer, gives spiritual gifts, enables witness, opens Scripture, and comforts
He seals salvation eternally, works through corporate worship, and grants discernment of truth
He sanctifies completely, removes all temptation, makes believers perfect, and grants eternal rest
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: He assures salvation, empowers character development, helps in prayer, gives spiritual gifts, enables witness, opens Scripture, and comforts

options: Exaltation; believers receiving rewards and honor in heaven for faithful Christian service
God completing salvation: being freed from temptation, made like Jesus, and receiving a glorified body for eternity
Immortality; the resurrection of all believers to live eternally with the Lord
Sanctification; the gradual process of God making believers increasingly more like Jesus
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God completing salvation: being freed from temptation, made like Jesus, and receiving a glorified body for eternity

options: Real Christians will continue in faith to the end and be kept by God's power for salvation
Once a person is saved, they are guaranteed to go to heaven regardless of behavior
Real Christians must obey God's commands to remain saved until the very end
Christians who stumble into sin can lose their salvation and be lost forever
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Real Christians will continue in faith to the end and be kept by God's power for salvation

options: A local congregation of baptized believers voluntarily joined together in covenant with Christ and each other
A denomination of congregations under pastoral authority exercising biblical church discipline
Any group of believers meeting in Jesus' name for corporate worship and prayer
The invisible universal fellowship of all believers in Christ throughout all history
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: A local congregation of baptized believers voluntarily joined together in covenant with Christ and each other

options: To protect Christian beliefs, preserve traditions, and prepare believers for Christ's return
To teach biblical doctrine, collect offerings, and discipline members who disobey God
To provide social services, comfort the sick, and build community among believers
To glorify God, observe ordinances, spread the gospel, and provide fellowship and accountability
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: To glorify God, observe ordinances, spread the gospel, and provide fellowship and accountability

options: Through Presbyterian councils representing all members and making major corporate decisions
Under apostolic succession and the authority of a bishop governing multiple congregations
Under the authority of a pastor empowered to lead and direct the congregation
Each congregation operates under Christ's Lordship through democratic processes with Christ as the Head
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Each congregation operates under Christ's Lordship through democratic processes with Christ as the Head

options: An impersonal spiritual force pervading the universe; eternal, all-knowing, but not personal
God is Spirit, personal, Creator distinct from creation, perfect, all-powerful and all-knowing
Creator superior to creation but limited in power and constrained by time
Transcendent Spirit, but limited in His knowledge of free human choices
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God is Spirit, personal, Creator distinct from creation, perfect, all-powerful and all-knowing

options: Pastors, deacons, elders, and bishops appointed by higher authorities
Pastors and deacons; pastor office limited to biblically qualified men
Elders and presbyters selected for life based on age
Pastors and ordained clergy chosen from the most educated members
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Pastors and deacons; pastor office limited to biblically qualified men

options: All churches that share the same theological and denominational beliefs
The leadership of all Christian denominations working together
The Body of Christ including all redeemed of all ages and nations
The Christian churches in a particular city or region
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The Body of Christ including all redeemed of all ages and nations

options: Believer's baptism: immersion beneath water in the name of the Trinity
Sprinkling water on believers in the name of the Father and the Son
Infant baptism: sprinkling or pouring water on people to cleanse from sin
Pouring water on baptized believers in the name of the Trinity together
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Believer's baptism: immersion beneath water in the name of the Trinity

options: No. Personal faith in Christ is sufficient; baptism is an optional symbolism
Only after confirmation and examination by church authority for full participation
Yes. Being a church ordinance, baptism is required to observe the Lord's Supper and before the privileges of church membership
Yes, but only after a period of spiritual growth and maturity demonstrated
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Yes. Being a church ordinance, baptism is required to observe the Lord's Supper and before the privileges of church membership

options: Baptism is only an outward symbol and has no spiritual significance or meaning
Baptism testifies that a person is already saved; it represents the Spirit's inward baptism bringing us into God's family
Baptism is required for salvation and brings the believer into union with Christ
Baptism is the sign and seal of God's grace accomplishing regeneration
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Baptism testifies that a person is already saved; it represents the Spirit's inward baptism bringing us into God's family

options: The believer's commitment to Christ and promise to live faithfully and obediently
Jesus' death and resurrection; believer's death to old life and raising to new life in Christ
The church's blessing of the convert and acceptance into Christian community
Christ's atoning work on the cross bringing forgiveness of sins and redemption
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Jesus' death and resurrection; believer's death to old life and raising to new life in Christ

options: Confirmation: the church's blessing upon baptized believers joining in full communion
Foot-washing: an ordinance showing Jesus' humility and command to serve one another
The Lord's Supper: a symbolic act of eating bread and drinking cup, remembering Christ's death
Fasting: abstaining from food to commemorate Christ's passion and show true devotion
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The Lord's Supper: a symbolic act of eating bread and drinking cup, remembering Christ's death

options: Any day chosen personally as one's own day of private worship and rest
Saturday, the Sabbath day ordained by God and never abolished for believers
Every day equally, since God's work and rest are now purely spiritual
Sunday, first day celebrating Christ's resurrection; a day for God, fellowship, worship, and pleasing activities
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Sunday, first day celebrating Christ's resurrection; a day for God, fellowship, worship, and pleasing activities

options: The spiritual power of God in believers' hearts; a present internal reality only
God's rule over all things; God ruling in believers' hearts now; to be completed when Jesus returns
The church as God's organization extending His rule through society and nations
God's future reign when Christ returns and establishes His visible earthly kingdom
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God's rule over all things; God ruling in believers' hearts now; to be completed when Jesus returns

options: Jesus will come again invisibly to remove believers before the final judgment
Jesus will return spiritually to believers' hearts and usher in new creation
Jesus will return to establish God's kingdom and bring peace on earth
Jesus will return personally and visibly in glory, raise the dead, and judge all people
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Jesus will return personally and visibly in glory, raise the dead, and judge all people

options: Three separate divine beings in eternal relationship but not united as one God
One God revealed in three different modes or forms at different times
Three Persons—Father, Son, Spirit—each fully God, not one-third; there is only one God
God the Father with two lesser divine beings, the Son and the Spirit
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Three Persons—Father, Son, Spirit—each fully God, not one-third; there is only one God

options: They will be annihilated and cease to exist eternally in nonbeing
They will be purified in purgatory before being allowed to enter into heaven
The unrighteous will be consigned to Hell, the place of everlasting punishment.
They will face God's judgment but some may receive His mercy and forgiveness
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The unrighteous will be consigned to Hell, the place of everlasting punishment.

options: Believers will receive power and rule with Christ over all the earth
The righteous in resurrected and glorified bodies, higher than angels, will receive reward and dwell forever with the Lord
The saved will enjoy eternal peace, rest from labor, and perfect communion
The redeemed will be transformed into spiritual beings without physical bodies
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: The righteous in resurrected and glorified bodies, higher than angels, will receive reward and dwell forever with the Lord

options: It is a spiritual realm beyond time and space, not a literal place
It is the place from which God reigns over the universe. It is a perfect place without sin or suffering
It is the future new creation where God will dwell with His redeemed people
It is God's present dwelling place where believers will go to be with Him
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: It is the place from which God reigns over the universe. It is a perfect place without sin or suffering

options: To win the lost by telling about Jesus and Christian example; every Christian should make disciples
To maintain personal holiness, pursue spiritual growth, and intercede for the lost
To witness by example, attend worship regularly, and encourage other believers
To serve the church faithfully, support missions, and live morally and honestly
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: To win the lost by telling about Jesus and Christian example; every Christian should make disciples

options: Traveling to other countries to convert people to the Christian faith
International mission work through sending missionaries to other countries for service
Preaching the gospel to unreached people groups in foreign lands and places
Evangelism to people of other cultures and languages; preaching the gospel to all nations
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Evangelism to people of other cultures and languages; preaching the gospel to all nations

options: Dedicating your life and resources to God's kingdom work and missions
Using your abilities and wealth to help the poor and needy in need
Managing God's resources—time, talents, possessions, Gospel—the way God wants
Giving money to the church and serving in church organizations and ministries
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Managing God's resources—time, talents, possessions, Gospel—the way God wants

options: Christians should give tithes, offerings, and alms according to their financial ability
Christians should give regularly to the church, to the poor, and to missions
Christians should sacrifice and give sacrificially until they have less than others
Christians should give to the Lord's work cheerfully, regularly, and generously. The more they make the more they should give
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Christians should give to the Lord's work cheerfully, regularly, and generously. The more they make the more they should give

options: God's creation; one man and one woman in lifetime covenant; children are a blessing
God's plan for couples to live together, have children, and build community
A social institution of one man and one woman with shared responsibilities
God's creation; two people united in love and commitment for life together
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God's creation; one man and one woman in lifetime covenant; children are a blessing

options: Parents and children share authority; discipline comes through natural consequences only
Parents exemplify God's plan, teach about God and values, discipline lovingly; children honor parents and learn biblical wisdom
Parents model Christianity and set clear rules; children ensure accountability together
Parents teach biblical values firmly, enforce strict rules; children obey out of respect
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Parents exemplify God's plan, teach about God and values, discipline lovingly; children honor parents and learn biblical wisdom

options: Yes, we are the true church; other denominations have departed from biblical truth
No, all Christian denominations are equally valid expressions of the Christian faith
No; salvation is through Jesus, not denomination; we cooperate with other Christians on mutual concerns
Salvation requires correct denominational affiliation and proper performance of baptism
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: No; salvation is through Jesus, not denomination; we cooperate with other Christians on mutual concerns

options: God rules the universe through secondary causes and natural laws alone
God is the Creator, Redeemer, Preserver, and Ruler of the universe.
God created the universe but is no longer involved with it
God preserves creation but other beings share in ruling it
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: God is the Creator, Redeemer, Preserver, and Ruler of the universe.

options: Yes, but personal experience is more important than doctrine and theology
Maybe, as long as people sincerely follow their own understanding of God
Yes; the Bible commands sound doctrine; right thinking leads to right living
No, what matters is personal faith and living a good moral life
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Yes; the Bible commands sound doctrine; right thinking leads to right living

options: A created being, the greatest of God's creatures, but not God Himself
Born of Mary by Joseph; adopted by God as His Son at baptism
Eternal Son of God, conceived by Holy Spirit, born of Mary, fully God and human
God's Son in spirit; He only appeared to have a real human body
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Eternal Son of God, conceived by Holy Spirit, born of Mary, fully God and human

options: He perfectly kept God's law except when it interfered with his mission
He lived a good life by human standards but had some failures
He kept the ceremonial law but broke the moral law for others
He obeyed all God's commandments and perfectly followed God's will
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: He obeyed all God's commandments and perfectly followed God's will

options: To teach us how to live by His example and moral teaching
Die on the cross as a substitute for our sins, securing forgiveness
To demonstrate God's love but not to actually pay for our sins
To show us how to overcome sin through our own effort and will
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.answer_choice: Die on the cross as a substitute for our sins, securing forgiveness

options: God is the Supreme Being worthy of all worship and praise
God is the eternal Creator of all that exists
God is the First and Chiefest Being
God is the most powerful and wisest of all beings
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God is the First and Chiefest Being

options: God's purpose to accomplish His plans through the exercise of human free will
God's Eternal Purpose according to the Counsel of his Will, whereby he foreordained whatsoever comes to pass
God's eternal foresight of all events that would freely come to pass in history
God's eternal permission allowing events to occur according to His sovereign will
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God's Eternal Purpose according to the Counsel of his Will, whereby he foreordained whatsoever comes to pass

options: By dipping only part of the body in water according to church practice.
By dipping in water but without regard to the name of Trinity.
By immersion or dipping the whole body in water according to Christ's institution.
By sprinkling or pouring water on the head according to church tradition.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: By immersion or dipping the whole body in water according to Christ's institution.

options: To join the most popular and culturally dominant church regardless of theology.
To remain independent and not commit to any church in their practice.
To give themselves to a particular orderly church and walk in commandments.
To participate in all churches equally without particular commitment to one fellowship.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: To give themselves to a particular orderly church and walk in commandments.

options: Believers alone; baptism is not required for worthy participation in communion
All baptized believers regardless of their current faith profession or repentance
Only those who make public profession and demonstrate mature spiritual sanctification
They who have been baptized upon a personal Profession of their Faith in Jesus Christ, and Repentance from dead Works
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: They who have been baptized upon a personal Profession of their Faith in Jesus Christ, and Repentance from dead Works

lead_in.question: What is the Lord's Supper?
lead_in.answer: The Lord's Supper is an Ordinance of the New Testament instituted by Jesus Christ; wherein by giving and receiving Bread and Wine, according to his Appointment, his Death is shewed forth; and the worthy Receivers are, not after a Corporal and Carnal manner, but by Faith, made Partakers of his Body and Blood, with all his Benefits, to their spiritual Nourishment, and growth in Grace.

options: Examine themselves for knowledge to discern the Lord's body and faith.
Examine themselves only for past sins without considering present faith and obedience.
Partake freely without any examination or requirement of repentance and obedience.
Come to the Lord's Supper without self-examination, trusting in church membership alone.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Examine themselves for knowledge to discern the Lord's body and faith.

options: Addressing God directly without the assistance of the Holy Spirit or Christ.
Offering our desires to God by the Spirit for things agreeable to his will.
Reciting prescribed formulas without genuine desire, confession, or thankfulness toward God.
Requesting whatever we want from God without regard for his will.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Offering our desires to God by the Spirit for things agreeable to his will.

options: The traditions of the church and the writings of church fathers guide prayer.
The whole Word of God directs us in prayer; especially the Lord's Prayer.
Personal feelings and individual preferences guide prayer more than Scripture or teaching.
Only the Psalms provide proper direction for what and how to pray.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The whole Word of God directs us in prayer; especially the Lord's Prayer.

options: To approach God with Reverence and Confidence as Children to a Father, and to pray with and for others
To confess our sins and ask forgiveness through Christ's intercession before God
To acknowledge God's holiness and recognize our unworthiness to approach Him
To recognize God as the sovereign ruler over all creation and all nations
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: To approach God with Reverence and Confidence as Children to a Father, and to pray with and for others

options: That God would reveal His nature fully and make Himself completely known
That God would enable us to glorify his Name in all whereby he maketh himself known and dispose all things to his Glory
That His kingdom would come and His will be done on the earth
That God would protect His name and prevent the misuse of His holy name
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: That God would enable us to glorify his Name in all whereby he maketh himself known and dispose all things to his Glory

options: That God's physical kingdom be established on earth with political power.
That our own personal wealth and power increase in this world.
That Satan's kingdom be destroyed and the kingdom of grace be advanced.
That the church become the dominant institution in all nations and cultures.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: That Satan's kingdom be destroyed and the kingdom of grace be advanced.

options: That God's will on earth mirror human preferences rather than heaven's order.
That God by his grace makes us willing to know and obey his will.
That God's will be forcibly imposed on the earth through human power.
That we be exempted from God's will if it conflicts with desires.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: That God by his grace makes us willing to know and obey his will.

options: Teaches us to take encouragement from God alone and to praise him.
Teaches to distribute praise between God and other spiritual beings or forces.
The conclusion emphasizes human worthiness and merit as basis for God hearing.
Indicates doubt whether God will hear us and advises trying multiple prayers.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Teaches us to take encouragement from God alone and to praise him.

options: He entered into a Covenant of Life with him, forbidding the Tree of Knowledge on pain of Death
He gave the law on pain of death; people could earn eternal life
He created humans with ability to choose good and evil; commanded obedience
He established a covenant of works offering eternal life for perfect obedience
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: He entered into a Covenant of Life with him, forbidding the Tree of Knowledge on pain of Death

options: Some ought to believe based on family tradition and upbringing in faith
Some have sufficient light from nature to clearly know that God exists
Every One ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great Sin and Folly who do not
People are obligated to seek God but may reasonably remain agnostic today
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Every One ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great Sin and Folly who do not

options: Guilt of Adam's sin; but his corruption of nature did not pass to us
Guilt of Adam's Sin, want of Original Righteousness, Corruption of Nature, and all actual Transgressions
Corruption of human nature only; we bear no guilt for Adam's original sin
Loss of original righteousness and natural tendency to sin; not inherited guilt
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Guilt of Adam's Sin, want of Original Righteousness, Corruption of Nature, and all actual Transgressions

options: By their Fall, Mankind lost Communion with God, are under his Wrath and Curse, liable to Death and Pains of Hell forever
By eating the fruit, Mankind lost innocence, faced God's anger, were exiled, and must suffer
By their Fall, Mankind lost the Garden, gained shame, became mortal, and need mercy
By their Disobedience, Mankind lost God's favor, face eternal judgment, earthly struggles, and separation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: By their Fall, Mankind lost Communion with God, are under his Wrath and Curse, liable to Death and Pains of Hell forever

options: God elected some and made salvation dependent on their free response to grace
God redeemed all mankind through Christ; therefore no one is left to perish
God left humanity to itself but offers salvation to all who earnestly seek
God from all Eternity elected some to Everlasting Life and made a Covenant of Grace to deliver them from Sin and Misery by a Redeemer
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God from all Eternity elected some to Everlasting Life and made a Covenant of Grace to deliver them from Sin and Misery by a Redeemer

options: Christ, the mediator between God and humans, truly human but not truly divine
The Lord Jesus Christ, the Eternal Son of God who became Man, being God and Man in two distinct Natures and one Person forever
Christ, God's Son, became human to reveal God's love and teach truth
Christ, God's chosen instrument, who was human like us in all respects
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Lord Jesus Christ, the Eternal Son of God who became Man, being God and Man in two distinct Natures and one Person forever

options: The offices of Apostle, High Priest, and Lord both on earth and in heaven
The roles of Teacher, Mediator, and Judge during his life and after his resurrection
The positions of Prophet, Shepherd, and Savior in his suffering and glory
The Offices of a Prophet, of a Priest, and of a King, both in Humiliation and Exaltation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Offices of a Prophet, of a Priest, and of a King, both in Humiliation and Exaltation

options: In revealing to us, by his Word and Spirit, the Will of God for our Salvation
In revealing all the Mysteries of God to us through his Spirit alone
By his Word alone, revealing all that God requires of Man in obedience
In teaching us the Law and the consequences of breaking God's Commandments
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: In revealing to us, by his Word and Spirit, the Will of God for our Salvation

options: In his continual Intercession for us and in revealing God's Will for salvation
In offering the sacrifices of the Temple on our behalf to God
In satisfying God's Justice through our repentance and continual Intercession for ourselves
In his once offering of himself a Sacrifice to satisfy Divine Justice, and making continual Intercession
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: In his once offering of himself a Sacrifice to satisfy Divine Justice, and making continual Intercession

options: In defending us from all Trials and establishing an earthly Kingdom for us
In subduing us to himself, ruling and defending us, and conquering all his and our Enemies
In ruling the Nations and conquering all his Enemies through earthly force
In subduing our Enemies through revealing God's Will and making us obedient to him
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: In subduing us to himself, ruling and defending us, and conquering all his and our Enemies

options: The works of creation clearly show God's existence equally to every person
Only through Scripture and the Holy Spirit can anyone truly know God
The Light of Nature and God's Works declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit do it fully and effectually for Salvation
Through reason and philosophy alone, or through Scripture without the Spirit's work
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Light of Nature and God's Works declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit do it fully and effectually for Salvation

options: His exercise of prophetic, priestly, and kingly offices with power over all things in heaven and on earth.
His resurrection in glory, His ascension to heaven, and His sitting at the right hand of God the Father.
Born in low condition, made under the Law, undergoing the wrath of God, the cursed death of the Cross, and burial.
His perfect obedience to the Law, His active and passive righteousness, and the satisfaction of God's justice.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Born in low condition, made under the Law, undergoing the wrath of God, the cursed death of the Cross, and burial.

options: His physical resurrection and His spiritual return to rule in believers' hearts
His ascension into heaven and His future coming to judge at the last day
His resurrection, His present seated session, and His reign in heaven eternally
His rising from the Dead on the third Day, ascending into Heaven, sitting at God's right Hand, and coming to judge the World
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: His rising from the Dead on the third Day, ascending into Heaven, sitting at God's right Hand, and coming to judge the World

options: By giving us the gift of saving faith and making us Children of God
By working Faith in us and thereby uniting us to Christ in our effectual Calling
By making us righteous and enabling us to obey his Law through the Spirit
By revealing Christ to us through his Word and sanctifying our hearts
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: By working Faith in us and thereby uniting us to Christ in our effectual Calling

options: God's grace making us aware of law, showing Christ's love, and transforming our desires
The Spirit's calling of sinners, revealing Christ's power, and strengthening our resolve to obey
God's work giving us faith, teaching us Scripture, and enabling us to live righteously
The Spirit's work convincing us of Sin, enlightening us in Christ, renewing our Wills to embrace him
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Spirit's work convincing us of Sin, enlightening us in Christ, renewing our Wills to embrace him

options: God's free Grace pardoning all our sins and accepting us as Righteous through Christ's imputed Righteousness, received by Faith alone.
God accepting us on the basis of our sincere repentance and our works of obedience to the Law.
Christ living a perfect life as our example, so we might follow His pattern and attain righteousness through imitation.
God making us inwardly holy and renewed through the transforming work of the Holy Spirit in progressive sanctification.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God's free Grace pardoning all our sins and accepting us as Righteous through Christ's imputed Righteousness, received by Faith alone.

options: The Spirit's action renewing our minds, freeing from sin's power, and empowering obedience
God's process of forgiving us, changing our hearts, freeing us from guilt and shame
The Work of God's Grace whereby we are renewed after God's Image, dying to Sin, living unto Righteousness
God's work making us holy, separating us from worldliness, and perfecting our nature entirely
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Work of God's Grace whereby we are renewed after God's Image, dying to Sin, living unto Righteousness

options: The Holy Scriptures are the Word of God and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience
Scripture is the Word of God, and the Church interprets it for us
The Scriptures contain the Word of God and are our guide for living
The Old and New Testaments, along with Church Tradition, are the Rule of Faith
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Holy Scriptures are the Word of God and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience

options: Their souls are made perfect in Holiness and pass into Glory; their bodies rest in graves till Resurrection
Their bodies are made perfect in Holiness and pass into Glory immediately
Their souls enter rest and their bodies are made perfect until the Resurrection
They are immediately judged and their souls are separated from their bodies
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Their souls are made perfect in Holiness and pass into Glory; their bodies rest in graves till Resurrection

options: Believers shall be acknowledged, but only their souls shall be made perfectly blessed
Believers shall be raised from the dead and wait for the Day of Judgment
Believers shall be made perfectly blessed but still face judgment and condemnation
Believers shall be raised up in Glory, openly acknowledged, acquitted at the Day of Judgment, and made perfectly blessed in Soul and Body in God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Believers shall be raised up in Glory, openly acknowledged, acquitted at the Day of Judgment, and made perfectly blessed in Soul and Body in God

options: Their souls are separated from God but their bodies are kept in Paradise
They sleep until the Day of Judgment when they shall be punished
Their bodies are cast into Torments but their souls rest in their Graves
Their souls are cast into the Torments of Hell, their bodies lie in Graves till Resurrection and Judgment
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Their souls are cast into the Torments of Hell, their bodies lie in Graves till Resurrection and Judgment

options: The Wicked shall be raised, separated from the Devil, and punished with torment
The Souls of the Wicked shall be sentenced while their Bodies remain in Graves
The Bodies and Souls of the Wicked shall be tormented but separated from Devil
The Bodies of the Wicked shall be raised, sentenced with their Souls to unspeakable Torments with the Devil and his Angels forever
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The Bodies of the Wicked shall be raised, sentenced with their Souls to unspeakable Torments with the Devil and his Angels forever

options: To honor God with all your being, keep his will, and help others as yourself
To obey God's commands with full devotion, honor his name, and serve others faithfully
To worship God completely, keep his law, and treat your neighbor with kindness and justice
To love the Lord our God with all our Heart, Soul, Strength, and Mind, and our Neighbour as ourselves
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: To love the Lord our God with all our Heart, Soul, Strength, and Mind, and our Neighbour as ourselves

options: I am your God who gave you the Law at Mount Sinai
I am the Lord your God who will bring you to the Promised Land
I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who brought you through the Wilderness
I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of Egypt, out of Bondage
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of Egypt, out of Bondage

options: God's Commandments are given to us so we may earn His grace
Because God is the LORD, our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his Commandments
We are advised but not bound to keep all of God's Commandments
God requires us to keep some Commandments because He is just and holy
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Because God is the LORD, our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his Commandments

options: All Men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Holy Scriptures
All men are permitted to hear the Scriptures preached but few are commanded to read
All men are exhorted to believe the Scriptures but not commanded to read them
Some men are permitted to read the Scriptures but most are not commanded
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: All Men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Holy Scriptures

options: To believe that God exists and to pray and read Scripture daily
To choose God as our personal Savior and commit our lives to serving him
To know and acknowledge God as the only true God, and to worship and glorify him
To honor God above all things and to obey all his Commandments
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: To know and acknowledge God as the only true God, and to worship and glorify him

options: Requires honoring God alone, forbids denying his existence, and demands true faith always
Forbiddeth rejecting God's authority, serving other powers, and disrespecting his holy name
Forbiddeth denying or not worshipping the true God, and giving his worship and glory to another.
Forbiddeth taking God's name in vain, creating idols, and worshipping false gods instead
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Forbiddeth denying or not worshipping the true God, and giving his worship and glory to another.

options: That the first Commandment requires us to honor God in everything
That we must keep God always before us in our minds and hearts
That God alone deserves our worship and praise above all creatures
That God sees all things and is displeased with having any other god.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: That God sees all things and is displeased with having any other god.

lead_in.question: What is forbidden in the first Commandment?
lead_in.answer: The first Commandment forbiddeth the denying, or not worshipping and glorifying the true God, as God, and our God; and the giving that Worship and Glory to any other, which is due unto him a alone.

options: Thou shalt not worship idols, nor create representations of God, nor pray to statues
Thou shalt not carve false gods, nor make altars to other powers, nor honor them
Thou shalt not build shrines to images, nor bow before them, nor offer them sacrifice
Thou shalt not make graven images or likenesses, nor bow down to them nor serve them.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Thou shalt not make graven images or likenesses, nor bow down to them nor serve them.

options: The receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances as God appointed
The performing of all religious duties, maintaining God's worship, and following scriptural ordinances
Following God's prescribed forms of worship, maintaining purity in religious practice and ordinances
Accepting and preserving all religious worship, ceremonies, and practices that the church ordained
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances as God appointed

options: The worshipping of God by Images, or any other Way not appointed in his Word
The making of images of God or the use of images in any worship
The breaking of idols and the refusal to worship any images at all
The worship of God in ways that man has invented and not God appointed
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The worshipping of God by Images, or any other Way not appointed in his Word

options: The LORD's power and dominion, his ownership of creation, and his jealousy for purity
God's authority over all things, his claim on us, and his demand for obedience
God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he hath to his own Worship
God's rule over us, his possession of our souls, and his care for true religion
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he hath to his own Worship

options: Requires respectful speech about God, honoring his law, and keeping his commandments strictly
Requireth holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, ordinances, word, and works.
Requireth treating God's name with respect, obeying his word, and worshipping sincerely
Demandeth reverence in prayer, proper use of God's ordinances, and obedience to his teaching
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Requireth holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, ordinances, word, and works.

options: What God is like and how we should worship him and serve others
How God created the world and the complete history of mankind from the beginning
The revelation of God, his Character, and all the Laws he demands of us
What Man ought to believe concerning God, and what Duty God requireth of Man
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: What Man ought to believe concerning God, and what Duty God requireth of Man

options: Requireth holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, and ordinances.
Forbiddeth making and worshipping of graven images and idols.
Forbiddeth the profaning and abusing of any thing whereby God makes himself known.
Forbiddeth denying the true God and giving his worship to another.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Forbiddeth the profaning and abusing of any thing whereby God makes himself known.

options: Breakers may escape Men's Punishment, but the Lord will not suffer them to escape his Righteous Judgment
Those who break it might escape human justice, but God's wrath will find them
Transgressors may face earthly consequences, but God's judgment is certain and eternal for all
Sinners may evade temporal punishment, yet the LORD's sentence is inescapable and just
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Breakers may escape Men's Punishment, but the Lord will not suffer them to escape his Righteous Judgment

options: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain.
Thou shalt not make graven images or likenesses of things in heaven or earth.
Honour thy father and thy mother that thy days may be long.
Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy: labour six days, seventh day rest.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy: labour six days, seventh day rest.

options: Before Christ's Resurrection, the seventh day; since then, the first day of the week.
The second day of the week is appointed to be the Christian Sabbath.
Before the Resurrection of Christ, God appointed the first day for the Christian Sabbath.
After the Resurrection of Christ, God appointed the sixth day to be the Sabbath.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Before Christ's Resurrection, the seventh day; since then, the first day of the week.

options: By resting from all work and labor completely on the Sabbath day
By ceasing all activities and remaining completely idle in holy contemplation
By holy Resting from worldly Employments, spending the Time in God's Worship, except Works of Necessity and Mercy
By spending the day in prayer and attending church services only
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: By holy Resting from worldly Employments, spending the Time in God's Worship, except Works of Necessity and Mercy

options: Forbiddeth the making and worshipping of graven images and likenesses.
Forbiddeth denying or not worshipping the true God and giving his worship to another.
Forbiddeth omission or careless performance of duties, and profaning the day by idleness.
Requireth diligent performance of the duties of the Sabbath and holy meditation.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Forbiddeth omission or careless performance of duties, and profaning the day by idleness.

options: The sixth day being the Sabbath and God claiming the seventh for people's employments.
God's allowing six days for lawful employments, claiming the seventh, his example, and blessing.
God's demanding constant labour six days and rest only for a portion of seventh.
God's forbidding work during the six days and allowing work only on seventh day.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God's allowing six days for lawful employments, claiming the seventh, his example, and blessing.

options: Thou shalt not kill or take away the life of thy self or neighbor.
Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy and do no manner of work.
Thou shalt not commit adultery or defile the marriage bed in any way.
Honour thy Father and thy Mother; that thy Days may be long upon the Land.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Honour thy Father and thy Mother; that thy Days may be long upon the Land.

options: Requireth holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, and ordinances.
Requireth preserving honour and performing duties in their several places and relations.
Forbiddeth the neglecting of or doing any thing against honour and duty in relations.
Requireth the omission and careless performance of duties during the Sabbath day.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Requireth preserving honour and performing duties in their several places and relations.

options: Requireth preserving honour and performing the duties belonging to every one in relations.
Forbiddeth neglecting or doing anything against honour and duty in places and relations.
Forbiddeth denying or not worshipping of the true God alone in all things.
Forbiddeth taking God's name in vain or swearing by it falsely.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Forbiddeth neglecting or doing anything against honour and duty in places and relations.

options: A Reward of health and blessing in the land to all who honor their parents
That God will grant length of days and success in life to the obedient
A Promise of long Life and Prosperity (as far as it serves God's Glory) to all who keep it
A Promise of earthly wealth and security to those who obey their parents faithfully
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: A Promise of long Life and Prosperity (as far as it serves God's Glory) to all who keep it

options: The sixth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not steal from thy neighbor".
The sixth Commandment is, "Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself".
The sixth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not bear false witness".
The sixth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not kill".
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The sixth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not kill".

options: To refrain from taking the lives of others and to protect all life equally
All lawful Endeavors to preserve our own Life, and the Life of others
Not to murder and to help those who are suffering from disease
To preserve life at all costs and to avoid all violence and conflict
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: All lawful Endeavors to preserve our own Life, and the Life of others

options: Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name.
Absolutely forbiddeth taking away our own life or our neighbor's life unjustly.
Forbiddeth all profaning and abusing of any thing whereby God makes himself known.
Forbiddeth all unchaste thoughts, words and actions of any kind whatsoever.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Absolutely forbiddeth taking away our own life or our neighbor's life unjustly.

options: Requireth lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of ourselves.
Requireth full contentment with our own condition and charitable frame toward neighbor.
Forbiddeth all unchaste thoughts, words and actions of any manner whatsoever.
Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in heart and behaviour.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in heart and behaviour.

options: Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name.
The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.
Forbiddeth taking away of our own or our neighbor's life unjustly.
Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in heart and behaviour.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.

options: Requireth maintaining and promoting truth between man and man and good names.
Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name.
Forbiddeth discontentment with our own estate and envying the good of neighbor.
Requireth lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of ourselves.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Requireth lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of ourselves.

options: The desiring of our Neighbour's possessions and all forms of greed and covetousness
All attempts to become wealthy and all worldly possessions and material gain
Whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly hinder our own, or our Neighbour's Wealth, or outward Estate
The stealing of property and the deliberate harm of someone's financial well-being
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly hinder our own, or our Neighbour's Wealth, or outward Estate

options: Thou shalt not lie or deceive anyone in matters of business or speech
Thou shalt not covet thy Neighbour's possessions or speak evil of him
Thou shalt not spread rumors or speak false information about anyone
Thou shalt not bear false Witness against thy Neighbour
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Thou shalt not bear false Witness against thy Neighbour

options: Requireth maintaining truth between man and man and of our neighbor's good name.
Requireth lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of others.
Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name.
Requireth full contentment with our own condition and charitable frame toward neighbor.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Requireth maintaining truth between man and man and of our neighbor's good name.

options: Requireth maintaining truth between man and man and of our neighbor's good name.
Forbiddeth discontentment with our own estate or envying the good of neighbor.
Forbiddeth taking away of our neighbor's life or whatsoever tendeth thereunto.
Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name.

options: Thou shalt not wish for thy neighbor's property, animals, or household possessions
Thou shalt not desire thy neighbor's possessions, wealth, or servants for thyself
Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house, wife, man-servant, nor anything that is his.
Thou shalt not lust after thy neighbor's goods, nor envy his estate or servants
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house, wife, man-servant, nor anything that is his.

options: Forbiddeth discontentment with our own estate or envying the good of neighbor.
Requireth full contentment with our own condition and charitable frame toward neighbor.
Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in all ways.
Requireth lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of others.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Requireth full contentment with our own condition and charitable frame toward neighbor.

options: Forbiddeth neglecting honour and doing anything against duty in their places.
Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name.
Requireth full contentment with our own condition and charitable frame toward neighbor.
Forbiddeth discontentment with our own estate, envying the good of neighbor.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Forbiddeth discontentment with our own estate, envying the good of neighbor.

options: Believers in Christ are able to perfectly keep God's commandments in this life.
All men are able to keep the commandments perfectly if they try hard.
No mere man since the fall is able to keep God's commandments perfectly.
Some men can perfectly keep the commandments through their own righteous efforts.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: No mere man since the fall is able to keep God's commandments perfectly.

options: God's Wrath and Curse, both in this Life, and that which is to come
Separation from God in this life and torment in the life to come
Death in this life and eternal separation from God's Love and mercy
Punishment from God now and condemnation at the Day of Judgment
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: God's Wrath and Curse, both in this Life, and that which is to come

options: Strict obedience to the law and perfect works to escape God's wrath.
Faith in Jesus Christ, repentance unto life, and diligent use of means.
Mere intellectual knowledge of God without faith in Christ or actual repentance.
Works and good deeds alone, without faith in Christ or repentance required.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: Faith in Jesus Christ, repentance unto life, and diligent use of means.

options: A saving grace through faith alone without actual turning from sin to God.
Complete freedom from all sin and perfect obedience in this present life.
Mere emotional sorrow for sin without true turning and purpose for obedience.
A saving grace from sense of sin and God's mercy turning to God.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.answer_choice: A saving grace from sense of sin and God's mercy turning to God.

options: His ordinances especially the Word, Baptism, the Lord's Supper, and Prayer.
Only the sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper alone for salvation.
All acts of piety that Christians perform without specific ordinance or institution.
The preaching of the gospel only, to the exclusion of all sacraments.

No, we should never swear any oath at all, by God or other powers
Yes, we may swear by the saints because God honors those who honor His people
Yes, but only by the angels who serve God and sit upon His throne
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. Lawful oath calls upon God alone, who knows our heart, to witness truth. No creature deserves such honour.

options: Show perfect obedience to parents and follow all their commands without ever questioning judgment
Show respect to parents but trust your own conscience more than their instruction
Honor your parents but you need not obey them if you disagree with commands
Show honour, love, and faithfulness to parents and authorities; obey their instruction; bear their weaknesses patiently; God governs us by them.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Show honour, love, and faithfulness to parents and authorities; obey their instruction; bear their weaknesses patiently; God governs us by them.

options: To refrain from personally killing but permit suffering and harm through your deliberate inaction
Not to dishonour, hate, injure, or kill in thoughts, words, or acts; put away revenge; don't harm myself; government prevents murder.
To show love to enemies and refrain from defending yourself or others from attack
To actively protect your neighbor's life and property from harm whenever possible and necessary
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Not to dishonour, hate, injure, or kill in thoughts, words, or acts; put away revenge; don't harm myself; government prevents murder.

options: God forbids the root of murder: envy, hatred, anger, and revenge, which He regards as murder.
God permits some anger and hatred if they do not result in actual violence
God condemns the act of murder but permits feelings of hatred in one's heart
God forbids murder but permits justified anger and revenge against those who harm us
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God forbids the root of murder: envy, hatred, anger, and revenge, which He regards as murder.

lead_in.question: What does God require in the sixth commandment?
lead_in.answer: I am not to dishonour, hate, injure, or kill my neighbour by thoughts, words, or gestures, and much less by deeds, whether personally or through another; rather, I am to put away all desire of revenge. Moreover, I am not to harm or recklessly endanger myself. Therefore, also, the government bears the sword to prevent murder.

options: We must love our neighbors but we are not obligated to show mercy to enemies
Yes, if we simply avoid murder and hatred we have fully satisfied God's requirements
No. God commands us to love our neighbour as ourselves, showing patience, gentleness, mercy, and doing good even to our enemies.
God commands us to show kindness only to those who treat us with respect and kindness
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God commands us to love our neighbour as ourselves, showing patience, gentleness, mercy, and doing good even to our enemies.

lead_in.question: But does this commandment speak only of killing?
lead_in.answer: By forbidding murder God teaches us that He hates the root of murder, such as envy, hatred, anger, and desire of revenge, and that He regards all these as murder.

options: God forbids outward acts of unchastity and immorality but permits private thoughts and secret desires
God forbids the act of adultery and unchastity but private thoughts and desires are not sinful
Since we are temples of the Holy Spirit, God forbids all unchaste acts, words, thoughts, desires, and whatever entices us to unchastity.
The seventh commandment forbids adultery and external unchaste behavior but permits private lustful thoughts alone
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Since we are temples of the Holy Spirit, God forbids all unchaste acts, words, thoughts, desires, and whatever entices us to unchastity.

lead_in.question: What does the seventh commandment teach us?
lead_in.answer: That all unchastity is cursed by God. We must therefore detest it from the heart and live chaste and disciplined lives, both within and outside of holy marriage.

options: God is merciful and will eventually excuse all sins, even serious ones against His majesty
God is just but His mercy means that all sins will be ultimately forgiven
God is merciful but also just. Sin against His majesty requires everlasting punishment of body and soul
God is merciful, therefore punishment for sin is temporary and limited in duration
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God is merciful but also just. Sin against His majesty requires everlasting punishment of body and soul

options: We should help the poor when they are truly worthy and clearly deserving of our aid
Help your neighbor but do not work excessively hard or earn too much money
Treat others well only when they treat you well and show you kindness first and foremost
Promote my neighbour's good, treat him as I wish to be treated, work faithfully to give to those in need.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Promote my neighbour's good, treat him as I wish to be treated, work faithfully to give to those in need.

lead_in.question: What does God forbid in the eighth commandment?
lead_in.answer: God forbids not only outright theft and robbery but also such wicked schemes and devices as false weights and measures, deceptive merchandising, counterfeit money, and usury; we must not defraud our neighbour in any way, whether by force or by show of right. In addition God forbids all greed and all abuse or squandering of His gifts.

options: Avoid serious and major sins, but small thoughts of sin are unavoidable and natural
Control your outward actions strictly but recognize private thoughts and desires cannot be regulated
No thought or desire against any commandment should arise; hate all sin with all heart and delight in all righteousness.
Try hard to avoid all sinful thoughts, and when they do arise immediately confess
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No thought or desire against any commandment should arise; hate all sin with all heart and delight in all righteousness.

options: The holiest can keep the most important commandments but will never fully obey them all
No. The holiest have only a small beginning of this obedience, yet earnestly begin to live according to all God's commandments.
Yes, the most holy and righteous believers can keep all God's commandments perfectly in this life
No, and therefore the righteous do not need to seriously try to obey all commandments
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. The holiest have only a small beginning of this obedience, yet earnestly begin to live according to all God's commandments.

options: To ensure we feel guilty about our many sins and work harder at righteousness
To frighten sinners into strict obedience rather than encourage them toward growth
So we become aware of our sin and seek Christ, and pursue good deeds and prayer, growing more in God's image.
So we will achieve perfect holiness and complete righteousness through our own human effort
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: So we become aware of our sin and seek Christ, and pursue good deeds and prayer, growing more in God's image.

lead_in.question: But can those converted to God keep these commandments perfectly?
lead_in.answer: No. In this life even the holiest have only a small beginning of this obedience. Nevertheless, with earnest purpose they do begin to live not only according to some but to all the commandments of God.

options: Prayer is optional for believers who have already received God's grace and full salvation
Prayer is less important than reading Scripture and performing good works for others
God gives grace and the Holy Spirit according to our own righteousness and merit
Prayer is necessary because it's most important to the thankfulness God requires; He gives grace and Holy Spirit only to those asking constantly.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Prayer is necessary because it's most important to the thankfulness God requires; He gives grace and Holy Spirit only to those asking constantly.

options: Pray with great emotion and feeling; repeat the same words many times; trust your own worthiness deserves answer.
Pray in private only; ask only for personal needs; believe God answers the worthy; use traditional set prayers.
Use fancy and beautiful language; ask God for worldly wealth and pleasure; show confidence in your prayer.
Call upon God revealed in His Word; know our need to humble ourselves; trust God hears for Christ's sake.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Call upon God revealed in His Word; know our need to humble ourselves; trust God hears for Christ's sake.

lead_in.question: Why is prayer necessary for Christians?
lead_in.answer: Because prayer is the most important part of the thankfulness which God requires of us. Moreover, God will give His grace and the Holy Spirit only to those who constantly and with heartfelt longing ask Him for these gifts and thank Him for them.

options: All the things we need for body and soul, as included in the prayer which Christ our Lord Himself taught us.
Only material blessings and health; we should never pray for forgiveness or spiritual growth.
Only what we truly deserve based on our good works and moral worthiness.
Only spiritual things for our souls; worldly things like food and shelter are sinful requests.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: All the things we need for body and soul, as included in the prayer which Christ our Lord Himself taught us.

options: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
Thou shalt have no other gods before Me. Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image or likeness of anything.
I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and in Jesus Christ His only Son, our Lord.
Our Father in heaven, Hallowed be Thy Name. Thy kingdom come. Give daily bread, forgive as we forgive, deliver from evil.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Our Father in heaven, Hallowed be Thy Name. Thy kingdom come. Give daily bread, forgive as we forgive, deliver from evil.

options: God's infinite mercy means His justice can be completely ignored and no payment needed
God demands that His justice be satisfied. Full payment must be made by ourselves or another.
We alone must make full payment ourselves and cannot receive help from anyone
God will accept partial payment for our sins if we truly and sincerely repent
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God demands that His justice be satisfied. Full payment must be made by ourselves or another.

options: To awaken childlike reverence and trust; God through Christ became our Father and gives us what we ask in faith.
To show respect to our earthly parents, who are the first representatives of God's authority and care for us.
To establish a formal distance and proper reverence, so we do not presume upon God's holiness with casual familiarity.
To acknowledge God as the Creator and Almighty Maker of all things, whose power transcends all earthly authority.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: To awaken childlike reverence and trust; God through Christ became our Father and gives us what we ask in faith.

options: To teach us that we must hope in the heavenly reward awaiting us after death and resurrection.
To indicate that God dwells physically in the heavens above and is separated from the earthly realm entirely.
Not to think of God's majesty in an earthly manner, and to expect all things we need from His almighty power.
To remind us of God's perfect government of all things in heaven, but not His rule over earthly matters.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Not to think of God's majesty in an earthly manner, and to expect all things we need from His almighty power.

options: That we are forgiven of our sins and our debts are pardoned by God's infinite mercy and compassion.
That we may rightly know God and sanctify Him in all His works; that our whole life honors rather than blasphemes His Name.
That God's kingdom grows mightily and rules all nations until His return in glory and power over all things.
That God rules us completely and we submit to His will in all earthly matters and spiritual concerns.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: That we may rightly know God and sanctify Him in all His works; that our whole life honors rather than blasphemes His Name.

options: That God would grant us earthly prosperity, success in our labors, and material abundance as signs of His favor.
That God would provide for us our daily needs for food, shelter, and security in this life.
That all people everywhere would honor and revere God's holy Name above all else and sing His praises.
God ruling us by His Word and Spirit, preserving His church, destroying the devil's works, until His kingdom comes.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God ruling us by His Word and Spirit, preserving His church, destroying the devil's works, until His kingdom comes.

options: For Christ's blood, do not impute our sins to us; evidence of God's grace is that we wholeheartedly forgive our neighbors.
For God's mercy, forgive all past and future offenses; evidence of grace is that we give abundantly to the poor.
For Christ's sake, grant us strength against temptation; evidence of God's love is that we remain steadfast in His Word.
For God's justice, do not allow our wickedness to remain; evidence of faith is that we confess all transgressions.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: For Christ's blood, do not impute our sins to us; evidence of God's grace is that we wholeheartedly forgive our neighbors.

options: Ask God to uphold us by His Holy Spirit since we are weak and unable to resist the devil, world, and flesh alone.
Ask God to prevent us from knowing sin and to keep us entirely free from all spiritual warfare.
Ask God to remove all difficult circumstances and trials that test our faith and commitment to His Word.
Ask God to deliver us from all physical evil and to grant us prosperity and health in earthly life.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Ask God to uphold us by His Holy Spirit since we are weak and unable to resist the devil, world, and flesh alone.
