options: Amen, meaning it is true and certain, expressing our confidence that God will grant what we have asked.
According to Thy will, O Lord, submitting all our requests to God's sovereign wisdom and perfect purpose.
For Thine is the kingdom, power, and glory forever. You are King over all, willing and able to grant our requests.
In the Name of Jesus Christ, our Savior and Redeemer, through whom all our prayers must pass to reach God.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: For Thine is the kingdom, power, and glory forever. You are King over all, willing and able to grant our requests.

options: So be it done, an expression of willing submission to God's will regarding all our requests.
The end of prayer, signifying that we have completed our petitions and are finished addressing God.
It is true and certain; God has more certainly heard my prayer than I feel my desire in my heart.
Let the covenant be sealed, confirming the binding agreement between God and His people.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: It is true and certain; God has more certainly heard my prayer than I feel my desire in my heart.

options: Certainly not. On the contrary, we daily increase our debt.
No, but we can help Christ to make the payment
No, our payment is impossible because our sins are infinite
No, only Christ can make the perfect payment for sin
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Certainly not. On the contrary, we daily increase our debt.

lead_in.question: Since, according to God's righteous judgment we deserve temporal and eternal punishment, how can we escape this punishment and be again received into favour?
lead_in.answer: God demands that His justice be satisfied. Therefore full payment must be made either by ourselves or by another.

options: No, but the angels are powerful enough to bear and endure God's eternal wrath
No. God will not punish another creature for man's sin, nor can any creature sustain God's eternal wrath
Yes, God can punish an innocent creature for man's sin if He should choose
No, because God will simply forgive man's sin without any payment being required
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God will not punish another creature for man's sin, nor can any creature sustain God's eternal wrath

options: One who is a true and righteous man and also true God, more powerful than all creatures
One who is a righteous angel or spirit, more powerful than humans but lesser than God
One who is truly God but need not necessarily be human or righteous
One who is human and filled with God's Holy Spirit but not truly God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: One who is a true and righteous man and also true God, more powerful than all creatures

options: He must be truly human so human nature can pay for sin, and righteous so He can pay for others
He must be human but need not be righteous, only willing to sacrifice Himself
He must be righteous but need not be human, as God's divine power alone is sufficient
He must be divine and powerful, but His righteousness depends on God's mercy and accounting
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: He must be truly human so human nature can pay for sin, and righteous so He can pay for others

options: By His divine mercy He forgave all sins and granted righteousness without bearing wrath
By His teachings He showed humanity how to bear God's wrath and gain eternal life
By His divine power He can bear God's wrath, obtaining and restoring for us righteousness and life
By His human nature alone He could endure God's wrath and obtain righteousness for us
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: By His divine power He can bear God's wrath, obtaining and restoring for us righteousness and life

options: The Holy Spirit given by God to provide wisdom and sanctification to believers
God the Father, who made all things and provides wisdom and redemption alone
The greatest human teacher who lived righteously and demonstrated the path to God
Our Lord Jesus Christ, whom God made our wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Our Lord Jesus Christ, whom God made our wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption

options: From the New Testament alone, which replaced the Old Testament and all its ancient prophecies
From Jewish tradition and the teachings of ancient prophets who predicted a coming Messiah
From the gospel: God revealed it in Paradise, proclaimed by patriarchs and prophets, foreshadowed in the law
From personal experience and the wisdom of great men about how to find salvation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: From the gospel: God revealed it in Paradise, proclaimed by patriarchs and prophets, foreshadowed in the law

lead_in.question: But who is that Mediator who at the same time is true God and a true and righteous man?
lead_in.answer: Our Lord Jesus Christ, whom God made our wisdom, our righteousness and sanctification and redemption (I Corinthians 1:30).

options: How to keep God's commandments perfectly; how to earn His favor; how to live righteously
How great my sins and misery are; how I am delivered from them; how to be thankful
God's love for me and all people; Christ's perfect example; the Holy Spirit's power
The Ten Commandments written in Scripture; the sacraments of the church; God's ancient promises
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: How great my sins and misery are; how I am delivered from them; how to be thankful

options: Only those who have been baptized and properly received the church sacraments are truly saved
No. Only those are saved who by a true faith are grafted into Christ and accept all His benefits.
Yes, because Christ died for all humanity and therefore all people are saved through His death
No, some are saved by faith in Christ while others are saved by their good works
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. Only those are saved who by a true faith are grafted into Christ and accept all His benefits.
True

options: Whatever brings personal comfort and hope based on our individual understanding of Scripture
What the church has determined and declared to be necessary for all true Christians
All promised in the Gospel, which the articles of Christian faith teach in summary
Only those teachings of the apostles which are clearly and directly written in the Bible
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: All promised in the Gospel, which the articles of Christian faith teach in summary

options: God's infinite power and majesty; Christ's teachings and example; the church's authority; moral living
The creation of the world; animal sacrifice; temple worship; priestly service; law giving
God the Creator; Christ's incarnation, suffering, death, resurrection; Holy Spirit; church; forgiveness; resurrection; eternal life
God's election of the saints; Christ's priestly office; spirit's baptism; church membership; resurrection
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God the Creator; Christ's incarnation, suffering, death, resurrection; Holy Spirit; church; forgiveness; resurrection; eternal life

lead_in.question: What, then, must a Christian believe?
lead_in.answer: All that is promised us in the Gospel, which the articles of our catholic and undoubted Christian faith teach us in a summary.

options: Into various parts based on each sacrament and how it individually applies to believers
Into three parts: God the Father and creation; God the Son and redemption; God the Holy Spirit and sanctification
Into two main parts: the teachings of the Old Testament and the New Testament faith
Into ten parts, one for each of the Ten Commandments and corresponding doctrine
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Into three parts: God the Father and creation; God the Son and redemption; God the Holy Spirit and sanctification

lead_in.question: What are these articles?
lead_in.answer: III.1.I believe in God the Father almighty, III.1. Creator of heaven and earth. III.2.I believe in Jesus Christ, III.2.His only begotten Son, our Lord; III.3.He was conceived by the Holy Spirit, III.3.born of the virgin Mary; III.4.suffered under Pontius Pilate, III.4.was crucified, dead, and buried; III.4.He descended into hell; III.5.On the third day He arose from the dead; III.6.He ascended into heaven, III.6.and sits at the right hand III.6.of God the Father almighty; III.7.from there He will come to judge III.7.the living and the dead. III.8.I believe in the Holy Spirit; III.9.I believe a holy catholic Christian church, III.9.the communion of saints; III.10.the forgiveness of sins; III.11.the resurrection of the body; III.12.and the life everlasting.

options: Because the three persons represent different roles that God plays in salvation
Because God revealed in His Word that these three distinct persons are the one, true God
Because human minds cannot comprehend one God, so we use three
Because the Father is God, but the Son and Spirit are not divine
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Because God revealed in His Word that these three distinct persons are the one, true God

options: God the Father is the Creator of all things, but it is Christ who upholds them
God the Father created all things long ago, but may not provide for our daily needs
The eternal Father has power over creation, but we should primarily trust our own ability
The eternal Father of Christ, Creator of all, who upholds all, is my God and Father in whom I trust
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: The eternal Father of Christ, Creator of all, who upholds all, is my God and Father in whom I trust

options: God's sovereign will by which He decrees whatever occurs and determines the course of all history
God's creative power by which He made all things and sustains them in perfect order
God's perfect foreknowledge by which He knows and ordains all things that will come to pass
God's almighty power by which He upholds all things and governs all creatures by His fatherly hand
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God's almighty power by which He upholds all things and governs all creatures by His fatherly hand

options: We can be patient in adversity, thankful in prosperity, and assured that God's love remains certain if we are faithful.
We should be patient in adversity, obey God in prosperity, and demonstrate through our faithfulness that we truly trust Him.
We can be patient in adversity, thankful in prosperity, and confident no creature shall separate us from His love.
We can be patient in adversity, thankful in prosperity, and demonstrate our righteous standing before God through our sincere obedience.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: We can be patient in adversity, thankful in prosperity, and confident no creature shall separate us from His love.

options: Because He took our punishment and rose from the dead to give us hope of heaven
Because He saves us from all our sins, and salvation is found in Him alone
Because He teaches us the way and example of how to live righteously before God
Because He loved us and gave Himself as a ransom to free us from bondage
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Because He saves us from all our sins, and salvation is found in Him alone

options: From the preaching of the gospel
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: From the law of God.

options: No, they show they don't truly know Jesus and have been misled by false teachers and superstitions
No, because they seek salvation through their own efforts instead of trusting in Jesus Christ alone
No, they deny that Jesus is the complete Saviour in whom all necessary salvation must be found
No, they show a lack of faith and understanding of who Jesus is and what He accomplished
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No, they deny that Jesus is the complete Saviour in whom all necessary salvation must be found

options: As God's chosen One, He is our Teacher of truth, our Intercessor with the Father, and our eternal Judge
As God's anointed, He is our Prophet revealing God's will, our Priest who redeemed us through sacrifice, and our eternal King
As God's servant, He is our Example showing holiness, our Redeemer paying the price, and our Lord forever
As God's representative, He is our Leader guiding us to salvation, our Mediator before God, and our Ruler
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: As God's anointed, He is our Prophet revealing God's will, our Priest who redeemed us through sacrifice, and our eternal King

options: Because I am a member of Christ by faith and share His anointing as prophet, priest, and king
Because I attend church regularly and participate in its sacraments faithfully
Because I believe in the teachings of Christ and live a moral life
Because Christ called His followers Christians during His earthly ministry to them
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Because I am a member of Christ by faith and share His anointing as prophet, priest, and king

options: Because Christ is the only One born of God, while all believers become God's children at baptism
Because Christ is God's only begotten Son by nature, while we become God's children through personal faith
Because Christ is God's unique Son by nature, and we are God's children through Christ's redemptive work
Because Christ alone is God's eternal natural Son, while we are children of God by adoption through grace
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Because Christ alone is God's eternal natural Son, while we are children of God by adoption through grace

options: Because He owns us by creation and redeems us from all enemies through His mighty power
Because He has authority over us as our supreme Master and demands our obedience and worship
Because He purchased our freedom from darkness and gave us authority to overcome sin in our lives
Because He ransomed us, body and soul, from sin and the devil's power with His precious blood
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Because He ransomed us, body and soul, from sin and the devil's power with His precious blood

options: God's eternal Son assumed true human flesh from the virgin Mary by the Holy Spirit's work, forever remaining wholly God
The Son of God became human born of the virgin Mary to demonstrate that sinless living is always possible
God's divine Son took human nature from the virgin Mary to show that God can dwell in human form
The eternal Son of God took on true human nature from the virgin Mary through the Holy Spirit, remaining true God, without sin
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: The eternal Son of God took on true human nature from the virgin Mary through the Holy Spirit, remaining true God, without sin

options: He is our Mediator and with His innocence and perfect holiness covers my sin before God
His innocent life shows us that sinless living is possible and teaches us how to overcome temptation
His holy birth and innocent life give us an example of perfect obedience and moral purity to imitate
His conception and birth in purity remove our guilt and enable us to become holy ourselves
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: He is our Mediator and with His innocence and perfect holiness covers my sin before God

options: That Christ experienced all our pain and sorrow to show His sympathy with our struggles and sorrows
That Christ bore God's wrath against the sin of humanity, and through His suffering as atoning sacrifice redeemed us
That Christ bore all our sicknesses and pain so we could be physically and spiritually healed
That Christ suffered greatly throughout His life to show us how to endure persecution and hardship faithfully
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: That Christ bore God's wrath against the sin of humanity, and through His suffering as atoning sacrifice redeemed us

options: Christ was sentenced by human authority to teach us that obedience to God matters most
Christ was condemned by an earthly court to show us that innocent people sometimes suffer unjustly
Though innocent, Christ was judged by Pilate to teach us to endure unjust treatment with patience
Though innocent, Christ was condemned by an earthly judge, freeing us from God's severe judgment
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Though innocent, Christ was condemned by an earthly judge, freeing us from God's severe judgment

options: Yes, the cross was reserved for criminals and slaves, proving He died as a condemned criminal
Yes, crucifixion was the most shameful death possible, showing that He suffered the worst punishment
Yes, being crucified meant He died the death that our sins deserved and that God required
Yes. Thereby I am assured that He took upon Himself the curse which lay on me
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Yes. Thereby I am assured that He took upon Himself the curse which lay on me

options: Love the LORD your God with all your heart and soul; love your neighbor as yourself
Keep all the ceremonial laws of Moses and maintain strict religious observances
Obey the Ten Commandments and avoid all external sins and wrongdoing
Believe in God truly and attend all religious services faithfully every week
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Love the LORD your God with all your heart and soul; love your neighbor as yourself

options: Because God's justice and truth required that satisfaction for our sins be made only through death of God's Son
Because God's holy law demands a death penalty for sin, and Christ's death paid that penalty
Because God's righteous nature demands payment for sin, and only the God-man could satisfy it
Because the infinite nature of God's majesty required a sacrifice of infinite worth to be made
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Because God's justice and truth required that satisfaction for our sins be made only through death of God's Son

options: His burial testified that He had really died.
So His disciples would have a tomb to visit after
So that He would rise from the dead on the third day
To fulfill the Old Testament prophecy about His death
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: His burial testified that He had really died.

options: Our death is the consequence of sin but no longer condemns us since Christ paid our debt
Our death is our final struggle with sin but leads to our resurrection and eternal home
Our death is not payment for our sins but ends sin and enters eternal life
Our death ends our earthly pilgrimage and begins our transition into the glory of God's presence
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Our death is not payment for our sins but ends sin and enters eternal life

options: Through Christ's death our old nature is crucified with Him so we may offer ourselves as a sacrifice to Him
Through Christ's death we gain power to overcome temptation and to live in righteousness always
Through Christ's death we are freed from all evil desires so we naturally love holiness
Through Christ's death our sinful flesh is put to death so we live only for God's glory
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Through Christ's death our old nature is crucified with Him so we may offer ourselves as a sacrifice to Him

options: That Christ went to the place of the dead to free the righteous souls held captive there
So that through His unspeakable suffering and agony, especially on the cross, Christ delivered us from hell's torment
That Christ actually descended to hell and experienced its torment to spare us from that punishment
That Christ underwent spiritual death and separation from God to redeem us from eternal condemnation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: So that through His unspeakable suffering and agony, especially on the cross, Christ delivered us from hell's torment

options: Christ's resurrection conquered Satan's power forever and guarantees that faithful believers will be raised up eternally
By rising from the dead Christ proved His divinity and promises that all believers will rise to eternal life
By His resurrection Christ overcame death, shares righteousness with us, raises us to new life, and pledges our glorious resurrection
Through His resurrection Christ won victory over death and evil, ensuring His followers will live forever
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: By His resurrection Christ overcame death, shares righteousness with us, raises us to new life, and pledges our glorious resurrection

options: That Christ was taken up into heaven before His disciples and is there for our benefit until He comes to judge
That Christ departed from His disciples and ascended to heaven to prepare a place for us to dwell
That Christ was lifted into heaven where He sits in glory and intercedes for us always
That before the eyes of His disciples Christ was taken up to heaven to await the day of judgment
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: That Christ was taken up into heaven before His disciples and is there for our benefit until He comes to judge

options: By His divinity Christ is everywhere and never absent from us; by His humanity He is gone.
Christ is with us spiritually through the Holy Spirit while His physical form departed and is in heaven
Christ's spirit is present with us always through faith while His body remains physically located in heaven
Christ's divine nature fills all things while His human nature remains now in heaven at God's right hand
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: By His divinity Christ is everywhere and never absent from us; by His humanity He is gone.

options: His divinity and humanity are completely separate natures not truly united in one person.
His divinity has no limits, is present everywhere, and is personally united with His human nature.
His human nature became unlimited and present everywhere after His ascension to heaven.
His divine nature alone is truly present everywhere; His human nature exists nowhere.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: His divinity has no limits, is present everywhere, and is personally united with His human nature.

options: He appears before God in our defense, guarantees our future resurrection, and gives us strength to overcome temptation
He intercedes for us constantly in heaven, ensures our salvation is secure, and empowers us to live holy lives
He pleads our cause before the Father, confirms our hope of heaven, and provides grace for us to pursue righteousness
Our Advocate in heaven; our flesh there pledges He will take us; Spirit sent enables us to seek heavenly things.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Our Advocate in heaven; our flesh there pledges He will take us; Spirit sent enables us to seek heavenly things.

options: No, nobody can keep God's law except Jesus Christ alone
No, I am too weak and need God's grace to obey
No, because sin blinds me to God's truth completely
No, I am inclined by nature to hate God and my neighbour.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No, I am inclined by nature to hate God and my neighbour.

lead_in.question: What does God's law require of us?
lead_in.answer: Christ teaches us this in a summary in Matthew 22: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it, You shall love your neighbour as yourself. On these two commandments depend all the law and the prophets.

options: Christ ascended to be separated from the earth and to await His return as judge of all
Christ ascended so He could be established as the eternal King ruling over heaven and earth forever
Christ ascended to His throne in heaven to be exalted in glory and authority over all creation
Christ ascended to manifest Himself as Head of His Church, through whom the Father governs all things.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Christ ascended to manifest Himself as Head of His Church, through whom the Father governs all things.

lead_in.question: How does Christ's ascension into heaven benefit us?
lead_in.answer: First, He is our Advocate in heaven before His Father. Second, we have our flesh in heaven as a sure pledge that He, our Head, will also take us, His members, up to Himself. Third, He sends us His Spirit as a counter-pledge, by whose power we seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God, and not the things that are on earth.

options: Through His Spirit He sanctifies us daily; through His power He strengthens us to overcome all temptation
By His Spirit He pours out heavenly gifts; by His power He defends us against all enemies.
By His grace He blesses us abundantly; by His might He protects us from all harm and danger
By His presence He comforts us constantly; by His authority He rules over and guards His church
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: By His Spirit He pours out heavenly gifts; by His power He defends us against all enemies.

options: Christ will return to judge all humanity impartially and assign eternal rewards or punishments accordingly
Christ will examine all people's deeds and determine who deserves heaven based on their moral goodness
Christ will judge all people fairly based on their works, rewarding the good and punishing the evil
Christ, who bore God's judgment for me, will judge my enemies and bring me to glory.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Christ, who bore God's judgment for me, will judge my enemies and bring me to glory.

options: He is true God; given to enable our faith in Christ, to strengthen us, and to remain in our hearts
He is true eternal God with Father and Son; given to share Christ with me, comfort me, and remain forever.
He is divine with the Father and Son; given to work within us, bless us, and keep us eternally
He is God's power at work in the world; given to make us holy and to guide our decisions
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: He is true eternal God with Father and Son; given to share Christ with me, comfort me, and remain forever.

options: Christ founded the church to teach the ways of salvation and to bring all people into His kingdom
Christ established the church as His body with a visible structure and leadership for all the faithful to follow
Christ gathers the church from all time through His Spirit and Word in true faith, and I'm a living member.
The church is the people whom Christ calls to worship together and to serve Him through loving others
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Christ gathers the church from all time through His Spirit and Word in true faith, and I'm a living member.

options: The church is where believers find fellowship and are equipped by Christ's gifts to build up the body
All Christians share the same spiritual gifts and blessings through their union with Christ in the church
Believers who are united in Christ share the privilege of salvation and work together for God's cause
Believers as Christ's members share in His treasures and gifts; everyone must use their gifts for others' benefit.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Believers as Christ's members share in His treasures and gifts; everyone must use their gifts for others' benefit.

options: God covers my sins with Christ's blood and then enables me to become righteous through faithful obedience
God forgives all my sins through Christ and gradually makes me righteous through His Holy Spirit's work
God won't remember my sins or sinful nature against me but grants me Christ's righteousness so I never face condemnation.
God accepts me through Christ and then helps me become holy by empowering me to obey His law
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God won't remember my sins or sinful nature against me but grants me Christ's righteousness so I never face condemnation.

options: Soul goes to Christ; flesh is raised by His power, reunited with soul, made like His glorious body.
My soul goes to heaven but my body remains sleeping in the earth eternally.
I will exist forever as a spirit in heaven completely without any body.
My body is raised purely spiritual and invisible, with no physical substance whatsoever.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Soul goes to Christ; flesh is raised by His power, reunited with soul, made like His glorious body.

options: I will someday reach perfect peace and joy when I depart from this world and enter God's presence
I now have joy in Christ; I will experience perfect happiness and dwell in God's eternal glory forever
I will later enjoy perfect peace and happiness forever in the presence of God in the heavenly place
I already feel eternal joy's beginning in my heart; I will possess perfect blessedness beyond perception and praise God forever.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: I already feel eternal joy's beginning in my heart; I will possess perfect blessedness beyond perception and praise God forever.

options: In Christ I am righteous before God and heir to life everlasting.
Through my faith in Christ I have earned my eternal life.
In Christ I am perfect in all my works and truly holy.
In Christ I am partially righteous and must hope for more righteousness.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: In Christ I am righteous before God and heir to life everlasting.

lead_in.question: What comfort do you receive from the article about the life everlasting?
lead_in.answer: Since I now already feel in my heart the beginning of eternal joy, I shall after this life possess perfect blessedness, such as no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor the heart of man conceived-- a blessedness in which to praise God forever.

options: No. God created man good and in His image in righteousness and holiness to know Him eternally
No, God made mankind good and in His image to have fellowship with Him and praise Him
No, God created humanity in His image to be stewards of creation and to have dominion over it
No, God fashioned man in His likeness to rule creation and enjoy an eternal relationship with Him
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God created man good and in His image in righteousness and holiness to know Him eternally

options: By my genuine faith in Christ and by becoming increasingly righteous through moral effort and sincere obedience
By faith in Christ combined with my good works that show my sincere commitment to living a holy life
By the work of the Holy Spirit making me righteous as I grow in holiness and obey God
Only by faith in Christ; God imputes Christ's satisfaction and righteousness to me as though I never sinned and fully obeyed.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Only by faith in Christ; God imputes Christ's satisfaction and righteousness to me as though I never sinned and fully obeyed.

options: Because faith connects us to Christ and His righteousness which becomes ours through our trusting in Him
Because faith accomplishes righteousness by connecting us to Christ who imparts His holiness to all believers
Because our faith in Christ brings us His perfect righteousness which God grants freely as His grace
Not because faith itself is righteous, but Christ's satisfaction and righteousness is my righteousness; I receive it by faith only.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Not because faith itself is righteous, but Christ's satisfaction and righteousness is my righteousness; I receive it by faith only.

options: God's law applies only to the Old Testament and no longer binds us.
God forbids good works and wants us to rest from all labor.
God's law requires perfect righteousness; our best works are imperfect and defiled.
Our works are imperfect but still count toward at least half of righteousness.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God's law requires perfect righteousness; our best works are imperfect and defiled.

options: The reward for good works comes through our own merit and labor.
God rewards the godly for their works out of obligation to them.
This reward is not earned; it is a gift of grace.
God only rewards those who perfectly obey all of His commands.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: This reward is not earned; it is a gift of grace.

options: No, although believers might struggle with producing fruit because they still battle with their sinful nature
Yes, many believers become careless about morality since they are assured that Christ paid for their sins
No, but sincere believers must strive hard to produce good works to ensure they remain grafted into Christ
No. It is impossible that those grafted into Christ by true faith should not bring forth fruits of thankfulness.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. It is impossible that those grafted into Christ by true faith should not bring forth fruits of thankfulness.

lead_in.question: But do our good works earn nothing, even though God promises to reward them in this life and the next?
lead_in.answer: This reward is not earned; it is a gift of grace.

options: From God's free choice and from our own personal decision to believe in Christ as our Savior
From the Word of God in Scripture and from the Holy Spirit working through our reason and understanding
From our parents' faith and from Christian education that teaches us to believe in Jesus as our Lord
From the Holy Spirit, who works it by the gospel and strengthens it through the sacraments.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: From the Holy Spirit, who works it by the gospel and strengthens it through the sacraments.

lead_in.question: Does this teaching not make people careless and wicked?
lead_in.answer: No. It is impossible that those grafted into Christ by true faith should not bring forth fruits of thankfulness.

options: Holy visible signs and seals instituted by God declaring and sealing forgiveness and eternal life through Christ's one sacrifice.
Holy means of grace established by Christ that mysteriously convey God's forgiveness and spiritual power to the faithful
Sacred ceremonies and rituals instituted by the church that remind us of Christ's work and Christian commitment
Outward religious ceremonies that symbolize our faith in Christ and demonstrate our dedication to the Christian life
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Holy visible signs and seals instituted by God declaring and sealing forgiveness and eternal life through Christ's one sacrifice.

options: Yes, they show us Christ's love and motivate us to live righteously and to pursue growth in holiness
Yes, the Holy Spirit teaches in gospel and assures by sacraments that our entire salvation rests on Christ's one sacrifice.
Yes, the gospel and sacraments both direct us to Christ and encourage us to trust in His eternal love
Yes, the Word and sacraments together guide our faith in Christ and help us grow in spiritual maturity
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Yes, the Holy Spirit teaches in gospel and assures by sacraments that our entire salvation rests on Christ's one sacrifice.

options: Seven: baptism, confirmation, penance, eucharist, unction, orders, and matrimony.
Three: baptism, the supper, and confirmation as practiced in the church.
Two: holy baptism and the holy supper.
One: only baptism, as the supper is merely a memorial meal.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Two: holy baptism and the holy supper.

options: Just as water cleanses the body completely, so the sacrament of baptism miraculously removes all our sins
Water cleanses dirt from the body, and baptism through God's sacramental action miraculously cleanses our soul
Water in baptism washes dirt as His blood and Spirit wash away all my sins, Christ's promise at His institution.
Baptism is an outward sign that we have already been cleansed inwardly and commit ourselves to Christ
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Water in baptism washes dirt as His blood and Spirit wash away all my sins, Christ's promise at His institution.

options: From Adam's original transgression in the garden, which separated all mankind from God and from eternal life
From the serpent's deception of Eve in paradise, which led to the entrance of evil into the world
From the fall and disobedience of Adam and Eve, by which our nature became corrupt and sinful
From Adam and Eve's sin in eating the forbidden fruit, which brought death to all of humanity
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: From the fall and disobedience of Adam and Eve, by which our nature became corrupt and sinful

options: Blood washes priests; Spirit washes believers; together they make us completely sinless.
Blood means outward cleansing; Spirit means inner peace and emotional comfort only.
Washed with blood means we never sin again; washed with Spirit means perfect knowledge.
Christ's blood washes away sins through grace; His Spirit renews and sanctifies us to live holy.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Christ's blood washes away sins through grace; His Spirit renews and sanctifies us to live holy.

lead_in.question: How does holy baptism signify and seal to you that the one sacrifice of Christ on the cross benefits you?
lead_in.answer: In this way: Christ instituted this outward washing and with it gave the promise that, as surely as water washes away the dirt from the body, so certainly His blood and Spirit wash away the impurity of my soul, that is, all my sins.

options: Christ established baptism as the means by which believers receive salvation and become members of His church
Christ commanded His followers to baptize people and assured them that baptism ensures salvation for all
Christ instituted baptism for all believers and promised that it grants salvation and forgiveness to the baptized
Christ instituted baptism, commanding to baptize all nations. He promises salvation to believers. Scripture calls it the washing of regeneration.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Christ instituted baptism, commanding to baptize all nations. He promises salvation to believers. Scripture calls it the washing of regeneration.

lead_in.question: What does it mean to be washed with Christ's blood and Spirit?
lead_in.answer: To be washed with Christ's blood means to receive forgiveness of sins from God, through grace, because of Christ's blood, poured out for us in His sacrifice on the cross. To be washed with His Spirit means to be renewed by the Holy Spirit and sanctified to be members of Christ, so that more and more we become dead to sin and lead a holy and blameless life.

options: Yes, water washes sins away, while the Spirit provides additional grace and comfort.
No, only the blood of Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit cleanse us from all sins.
Yes, water itself has cleansing power when used in baptism by a priest.
Yes, but only if the person being baptized has perfect faith and repentance.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No, only the blood of Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit cleanse us from all sins.

lead_in.question: Where has Christ promised that He will wash us with His blood and Spirit as surely as we are washed with the water of baptism?
lead_in.answer: In the institution of baptism, where He says: Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. He who believes and is baptized will be saved, but he who does not believe will be condemned. This promise is repeated where Scripture calls baptism the washing of regeneration and the washing away of sins.

options: God declares that through baptism the water magically transforms us so that all our sins are completely erased
God wants us to know that baptism physically removes the stains of sin just as water removes dirt
God teaches blood and Spirit remove sins like water removes dirt, and assures us we're truly cleansed spiritually as bodily.
The Holy Spirit teaches that baptism is a powerful means through which God actually cleanses us from sin
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: God teaches blood and Spirit remove sins like water removes dirt, and assures us we're truly cleansed spiritually as bodily.

options: Yes, infants must be baptized immediately so they can receive God's grace and be part of God's covenant
Yes, infants belong to God's covenant and receive redemption and Spirit; baptism grafts them into the church replacing circumcision.
Yes, infants should be baptized because they belong to believing Christian parents who claim them for God's family
Yes, infants of Christian parents need baptism so they are marked as God's people and saved from sin
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Yes, infants belong to God's covenant and receive redemption and Spirit; baptism grafts them into the church replacing circumcision.

options: Christ instructs us to partake of bread and wine in remembrance; through this meal He feeds our souls with divine grace
Commands remembrance through eating bread and drinking cup; His body and blood nourish my soul as surely as I receive these signs.
Christ commanded us to eat the bread and drink the cup to remember His death; these elements truly are His body and blood
Commands remembrance of His sacrifice through this sacred meal; the bread and wine are His actual flesh and blood present
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Commands remembrance through eating bread and drinking cup; His body and blood nourish my soul as surely as I receive these signs.

options: To accept Christ's suffering and death for forgiveness and be united with His body through the Spirit.
To believe that Christ's literal body is present in the bread and wine through the priest's blessing.
To accept Christ's suffering by faith while remaining spiritually separate from His body until heaven.
To commemorate Christ's death through eating bread and wine as reminders and symbols only.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: To accept Christ's suffering and death for forgiveness and be united with His body through the Spirit.

lead_in.question: How does the Lord's Supper signify and seal to you that you share in Christ's one sacrifice on the cross and in all His gifts?
lead_in.answer: In this way: Christ has commanded me and all believers to eat of this broken bread and drink of this cup in remembrance of Him. With this command He gave these promises: First, as surely as I see with my eyes the bread of the Lord broken for me and the cup given to me, so surely was His body offered for me and His blood poured out for me on the cross. Second, as surely as I receive from the hand of the minister and taste with my mouth the bread and the cup of the Lord as sure signs of Christ's body and blood, so surely does He Himself nourish and refresh my soul to everlasting life with His crucified body and shed blood.

options: At the Lord's Supper institution, Christ commands remembrance through bread and wine; Scripture calls it participation in His body and blood.
At Pentecost when the Holy Spirit was given to believers at the breaking of bread.
At the Transfiguration where Christ was glorified with Moses and Elijah, eating and drinking with them.
In the feeding of the five thousand where Christ multiplied loaves and fishes for the multitude.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: At the Lord's Supper institution, Christ commands remembrance through bread and wine; Scripture calls it participation in His body and blood.

lead_in.question: What does it mean to eat the crucified body of Christ and to drink His shed blood?
lead_in.answer: First, to accept with a believing heart all the suffering and the death of Christ, and so receive forgiveness of sins and life eternal. Second, to be united more and more to His sacred body through the Holy Spirit, who lives both in Christ and in us. Therefore, although Christ is in heaven and we are on earth, yet we are flesh of His flesh and bone of His bones, and we forever live and are governed by one Spirit, as the members of our body are by one soul.

options: Yes. Through the priest's consecration the bread is transformed into the real body of Christ.
No. But the bread becomes Christ's body through God's power even though nothing appears to change.
No. Water isn't changed to blood in baptism; bread isn't changed to body in supper but is called so sacramentally.
Yes. Though it remains bread in appearance, the substance is miraculously changed into Christ's body.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. Water isn't changed to blood in baptism; bread isn't changed to body in supper but is called so sacramentally.

options: The bread and wine are merely symbols of Christ's body and blood with no real spiritual significance to believers
The bread and wine physically transform into His body and blood through the priest's consecration for literal consumption
Through priestly blessing, Christ's body is daily re-offered for the sins of both living and dead
Bread nourishes bodies as His body nourishes souls eternally; by Spirit we truly share in Him and His suffering becomes ours.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Bread nourishes bodies as His body nourishes souls eternally; by Spirit we truly share in Him and His suffering becomes ours.

options: Yes, unless we are regenerated by the Spirit of God.
No, we can do some good works through natural strength
Yes, but we can gradually improve ourselves through moral effort
Yes, but God will eventually forgive even such corruption through grace
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Yes, unless we are regenerated by the Spirit of God.

options: The mass teaches that complete forgiveness comes only through daily priest-offered sacrifice, not through Christ's one historical death
The Lord's Supper and the mass are essentially the same, both offering Christ's sacrifice daily for the living and dead
Supper witnesses complete forgiveness through Christ's one sacrifice; mass wrongly teaches daily re-offering and worship of Christ bodily present in bread.
Both Supper and mass teach that Christ is present in the bread and wine to be worshipped by believers
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Supper witnesses complete forgiveness through Christ's one sacrifice; mass wrongly teaches daily re-offering and worship of Christ bodily present in bread.

options: Those who have confessed their sins to the minister and promise to endeavor to live better.
Those displeased with sins yet trusting in their forgiveness, covered by Christ, desiring to strengthen faith and amend life. Hypocrites and unrepentant eat judgment.
Only the spiritually mature and morally pure who have overcome their greatest temptations and weaknesses.
All baptized members of the Christian church who profess belief in Christ and are confirmed communicants.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Those displeased with sins yet trusting in their forgiveness, covered by Christ, desiring to strengthen faith and amend life. Hypocrites and unrepentant eat judgment.

options: No. The covenant would be profaned and God's wrath kindled. The church must exclude them by ecclesiastical discipline.
No, but the church should admit them secretly to avoid seeming harsh or judgmental toward them.
Yes. The supper should be offered to all as a means toward their eventual conversion.
Only if they refuse to repent; those showing some signs of faith should be permitted.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. The covenant would be profaned and God's wrath kindled. The church must exclude them by ecclesiastical discipline.

lead_in.question: Who are to come to the table of the Lord?
lead_in.answer: Those who are truly displeased with themselves because of their sins and yet trust that these are forgiven them and that their remaining weakness is covered by the suffering and death of Christ, and who also desire more and more to strengthen their faith and amend their life. But hypocrites and those who do not repent eat and drink judgment upon themselves.

options: The authority of priests alone to forgive sins and administer the sacraments to cleanse the congregation
The apostle Peter alone, to whom Christ gave the exclusive keys to bind and loose all sins eternally
Gospel preaching and church discipline. These open the kingdom to believers and close it to unbelievers.
Prayer and fasting by the church leaders, by which the kingdom is spiritually opened to the worthy
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Gospel preaching and church discipline. These open the kingdom to believers and close it to unbelievers.

options: Gospel opens the kingdom by proclaiming God's forgiveness to believers; closes it by proclaiming His wrath on unbelievers who don't repent.
The gospel declares that believers receive automatic forgiveness without repentance, while unbelievers face eternal separation from God's presence
The gospel proclaims forgiveness to all people indiscriminately, promising that God's love prevents any from experiencing His eternal wrath
Gospel preaching by the church opens the kingdom only to those who receive the sacraments from authorized priests
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Gospel opens the kingdom by proclaiming God's forgiveness to believers; closes it by proclaiming His wrath on unbelievers who don't repent.

options: Church discipline immediately excommunicates those who sin without any chance for repentance or restoration to the church community
Members showing unchristian behavior should be privately criticized by elders but allowed to continue receiving all church sacraments
Unchristian members are admonished, reported to elders, forbidden sacraments, and excluded. They're received back when they show real amendment.
Sinful church members are permanently barred from the church once admonished, never permitted to return regardless of their later repentance
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Unchristian members are admonished, reported to elders, forbidden sacraments, and excluded. They're received back when they show real amendment.

options: We do good works because Christ's redemption obligates us to keep God's law perfectly to maintain our salvation
Show thankfulness to God and praise Him; assure ourselves of faith by its fruits; win neighbors to Christ by godly living.
Good works are necessary to earn God's favor, since our justification depends on the quality of our righteous deeds
Good works are optional displays of superior piety for Christians, but are not required by God for any believer
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Show thankfulness to God and praise Him; assure ourselves of faith by its fruits; win neighbors to Christ by godly living.

options: Only those who refuse to turn are lost; those who once believed keep their salvation.
Yes. God's mercy and Christ's sacrifice forgive all sins regardless of the sinner's repentance.
By no means. No unchaste person, idolater, adulterer, thief, greedy person, drunkard, slanderer, or robber shall inherit God's kingdom.
Yes. If they have faith alone they will be saved despite their continued impenitent lifestyle.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: By no means. No unchaste person, idolater, adulterer, thief, greedy person, drunkard, slanderer, or robber shall inherit God's kingdom.

options: Repentance is making satisfaction and payment to God for our sinful acts.
Repentance is obeying God's law perfectly for the rest of our life on earth.
It is the dying of the old nature and the coming to life of the new.
Repentance is feeling deep remorse and sorrow for the sins we have committed.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: It is the dying of the old nature and the coming to life of the new.

options: To feel deep regret for the consequences of sin but without necessarily rejecting sin itself as offensive to God
To grieve with heartfelt sorrow that we offended God by sin, and increasingly to hate and flee from it.
To recognize that sinning is wrong in theory while continuing to practice sin with an understanding that grace covers it
To temporarily mourn one's sins while aware they will be forgiven, and then gradually to move beyond the grief
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: To grieve with heartfelt sorrow that we offended God by sin, and increasingly to hate and flee from it.

options: No. God created man able to obey. Man's disobedience robbed all descendants of these gifts
No, humans still retain the ability to perfectly obey God's law despite the fall if they try very hard
Yes, God's law is unjust because He requires what humans cannot naturally accomplish without divine grace assistance always
No, God created all people with enough power to obey if they educate themselves in God's moral law
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God created man able to obey. Man's disobedience robbed all descendants of these gifts

options: The determination to obey God's law through human effort and willpower, demonstrating one's superior righteousness compared to others
The feeling of satisfaction that comes from successfully performing good works and receiving praise from Christian community members
Heartfelt joy in God through Christ, and love and delight to live according to God's will in all good works.
A temporary emotional high when experiencing God's blessings, which gradually fades as life's difficulties and challenges accumulate
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Heartfelt joy in God through Christ, and love and delight to live according to God's will in all good works.

options: Works that comply with church traditions and the teachings of learned religious leaders, even if Scripture seems to suggest otherwise
Works that accomplish much good in society and receive approval from communities, regardless of the religious motives behind them
Works that feel morally right to our conscience, whether or not they align with specific biblical commands or principles
Works from true faith, according to God's law, to His glory, not based on our opinions or human precepts.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Works from true faith, according to God's law, to His glory, not based on our opinions or human precepts.

options: The ceremonial laws of Moses regarding sacrifices, feasts, and temple worship.
The Ten Commandments of God revealed to Moses at Mount Sinai.
The laws of Christ summed up in the twofold command to love.
The civil laws of Israel for governing their kingdom and their nation.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: The Ten Commandments of God revealed to Moses at Mount Sinai.

options: Into ten parts, one for each commandment, each with its own purpose and reason.
Into two parts: external actions and internal thoughts and desires of the heart.
Into three parts: our duties to God, to ourselves, and to our neighbors.
Into two parts: first, how to live toward God; second, our duties toward our neighbour.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Into two parts: first, how to live toward God; second, our duties toward our neighbour.

lead_in.question: What is the law of the LORD?
lead_in.answer: God spoke all these words, saying: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. 1. You shall have no other gods before Me. 2. You shall not make for yourself a graven image, 2. or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, 2. or that is in the earth beneath, 2. or that is in the water under the earth; 2. you shall not bow down to them or serve them; 2. for I the LORD your God am a jealous God, 2. visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children 2. to the third and fourth generation 2. of those who hate Me, 2. but showing steadfast love to thousands of those 2. who love Me and keep My commandments. 3. You shall not take the Name of the LORD your God 3. in vain; 3. for the LORD will not hold him guiltless 3. who takes His Name in vain. 4. Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. 4. Six days you shall labour, and do all your work; 4. but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your 4. God; 4. in it you shall not do any work, 4. you, or your son, or your daughter, 4. your manservant, or your maidservant, 4. or your cattle, 4. or the sojourner who is within your gates; 4. for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, 4. the sea, and all that is in them, 4. and rested the seventh day; 4. therefore the LORD blessed the sabbath day 4. and hallowed it. 5. Honour your father and your mother, 5. that your days may be long 5. in the land which the LORD your God gives you. 6. You shall not kill. 7. You shall not commit adultery. 8. You shall not steal. 9. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbour. 10. you shall not covet your neighbour's house; 10. you shall not covet your neighbour's wife, 10. or his manservant, or his maidservant, 10. or his ox, or his ass, 10. or anything that is your neighbour's.

options: Trust and obey the one God while maintaining loyalty to family, nation, and personal ambitions within reasonable limits always
Believe that God exists, avoid speaking His name irreverently, and acknowledge Him publicly without necessarily obeying all His commands
Acknowledge that God is supreme while respecting other religions' worship practices and integrating their wisdom into your personal faith
Flee idolatry; know, trust, and submit to the only God alone; love, fear, and honour Him with all heart; forsake all rather than disobey.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Flee idolatry; know, trust, and submit to the only God alone; love, fear, and honour Him with all heart; forsake all rather than disobey.

options: Refusing to worship any god because of doubt about God's existence or the reliability of Scripture's testimony about Him
Having or inventing something to trust in instead of or along with the only true God revealed in His Word.
Making carved statues or images to represent God for use in worship, which directly violates His command against graven idols
Worshipping God while also respecting the religious practices and deities honored by other cultures and nations as equally valid
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: Having or inventing something to trust in instead of or along with the only true God revealed in His Word.

options: Images of any kind are prohibited absolutely, including images of creatures and saints, because all represent turning from God
Yes, we may make images of God for churches to help people understand divine nature and to aid in worship
We may make images of creatures but are forbidden from making any images whatsoever, since all image-making displeases God
No. God cannot be visibly portrayed. Creatures may be portrayed, but forbidden for worship or serving God through them.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God cannot be visibly portrayed. Creatures may be portrayed, but forbidden for worship or serving God through them.

options: The church may use images for instruction, though preaching is also necessary.
Yes, images teach the unlettered laity more effectively than any preaching.
Images may be tolerated in churches but never worshipped or honoured.
No. God wants His people taught by living preaching of His Word, not by dumb images.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:heidelbe.answer_choice: No. God wants His people taught by living preaching of His Word, not by dumb images.

options: Three persons in the Godhead—Father, Son, Spirit—one God in essence and power
One divine person manifesting in three different roles—as Father in creation, Son in redemption, Spirit in sanctification of believers
The Father is God; the Son and Spirit are created beings subordinate to the Father's authority and power
Four distinct divine persons unified in authority, the Father, Son, Spirit, and a fourth divine principle or emanation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Three persons in the Godhead—Father, Son, Spirit—one God in essence and power

options: The universal congregation of all believers throughout history who have true faith, regardless of doctrine or practice
A social organization dedicated to moral improvement and community service in the name of Christian faith and ideals
An institution governed by church leaders whose traditions and teachings guide believers in their understanding of Scripture
The organized society of professing believers where the Gospel is truly preached and ordinances rightly administered
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The organized society of professing believers where the Gospel is truly preached and ordinances rightly administered

options: We request God to provide only spiritual blessing while avoiding concern for physical food and daily necessities
We ask God to give us unlimited abundance and all material desires we seek throughout our lifetime
We petition God to grant us material success and pleasure as evidence of His favor toward us
We pray for a competent portion of life's good things and God's blessing
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: We pray for a competent portion of life's good things and God's blessing

options: We request that God forgive us our debts while we withhold forgiveness from those who owe us harm
We pray that God removes our guilt only after we demonstrate sufficient personal repentance and self-punishment for sins
We ask God to forgive us only if we first achieve perfect forgiveness toward all others who wronged us
We pray God would freely pardon our sins, encouraged because He enables us to forgive
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: We pray God would freely pardon our sins, encouraged because He enables us to forgive

options: We request protection from evil by depending entirely on our own moral strength and willpower to resist
We ask God to ensure we never experience any temptation, struggle, or difficulty in our Christian journey
We pray God would either keep us from temptation or support us when tempted
We pray that God removes all testing and difficulty from life, because temptation indicates His displeasure with us
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: We pray God would either keep us from temptation or support us when tempted

options: God's decrees are accomplished through human free will and choice
God executes His decrees only through the laws of nature
God's decrees are carried out by angels and spiritual beings alone
God executes His decrees in the works of creation and providence.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God executes His decrees in the works of creation and providence.

options: God's making all things from nothing by the word of His power.
An eternal process of self-organization of pre-existing matter into visible forms.
The natural unfolding of divine potential through impersonal forces without direction.
God's arranging and organizing already-existing material over many ages of time.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God's making all things from nothing by the word of His power.

options: As immortal spirits inhabiting material bodies without responsibility for the creation.
After the image of the angels and heavenly beings, though inferior in nature.
God created man male and female in His image, in knowledge and holiness.
In the divine image but later corrupted by Satan before completion.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God created man male and female in His image, in knowledge and holiness.

options: God's setting the universe in motion and allowing natural laws to operate.
The universe operating entirely through chance and random events without divine direction.
God's most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all creatures.
God's plan for a distant future but not involvement in daily affairs.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God's most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all creatures.

options: They were tempted by Satan and deceived but not truly guilty of sin by their choice.
Our first parents fell from the estate wherein they were created by sinning against God
They sinned and fell but immediately received the promise of Christ to restore their estate.
They remained unfallen in essence but lost some privileges and special gifts God had granted them.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Our first parents fell from the estate wherein they were created by sinning against God

options: Unintentional error and weakness in attempting to follow moral law
Behavior that violates human moral standards and civil laws
Any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, God's law
Deliberate choice to break God's stated commands through willful sinful rebellion
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, God's law

options: To achieve happiness and success in all worldly pursuits
To serve mankind and build a perfect society on earth
To acquire knowledge and develop our natural talents and abilities
Man's chief end is to glorify God and to enjoy Him forever
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Man's chief end is to glorify God and to enjoy Him forever

options: All mankind, descending from Adam, sinned in him and fell with him
All mankind chose to sin independently like Adam did
Only Adam sinned; the rest of mankind inherit the consequence
Only those who consciously choose to sin are held responsible
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: All mankind, descending from Adam, sinned in him and fell with him

options: Christ was born a normal human and later adopted into divine sonship when the Spirit descended at baptism
The eternal Christ-Spirit became human in Jesus while not truly possessing a body or suffering any human limitation
Christ took a true body and soul, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of Mary
Christ took a human body from Mary but possessed a divine spirit rather than a human soul
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Christ took a true body and soul, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of Mary

options: Justification and adoption only, for these are the primary work of the Holy Spirit in salvation.
They partake of justification, adoption, sanctification, and the several benefits which accompany or flow from them
Sanctification and perseverance in grace, by which believers are cleansed from all remaining corruption.
Grace and assurance only, for these are the immediate effects of God's saving work.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: They partake of justification, adoption, sanctification, and the several benefits which accompany or flow from them

options: An act of God's free grace whereby we are received as sons of God
A legal process where we earn the right to be God's children
A state we achieve through perfect obedience to God's law
The natural result of being born into a Christian family
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: An act of God's free grace whereby we are received as sons of God

options: Wealth and earthly prosperity, good health, long life, and protection from all suffering and trial.
Visible miracles and supernatural powers, special revelations, and clear signs of God's favor.
Freedom from all temptation, complete moral perfection, and victory over every human weakness.
Assurance of God's love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, increase of grace, and perseverance
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Assurance of God's love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, increase of grace, and perseverance

options: God requires man's obedience to His revealed will
To strive to do whatever makes us happy and fulfilled
To obey the moral law we discover through our own reason
To follow the teachings of religious leaders and traditions
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: God requires man's obedience to His revealed will

options: A civil law for governing the ancient Jewish nation
The moral law God revealed to man for his obedience
The natural law written in man's conscience and reason
A ceremonial law to be observed in the tabernacle
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The moral law God revealed to man for his obedience

options: The moral law is found in the ceremonial laws of the Old Testament
The moral law is summarized in the Sermon on the Mount
The moral law is summarily comprehended in the Ten Commandments.
The moral law is revealed through nature and human conscience alone
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the Ten Commandments.

options: The testimony of early church fathers alone confirms the Bible's authority
Scientific evidence and historical research prove the Bible is God's Word
We know the Bible is God's Word because it never contradicts itself
The Spirit of God bearing witness in our hearts persuades us the Bible is God's Word
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The Spirit of God bearing witness in our hearts persuades us the Bible is God's Word

options: Thou shalt love God with all thy heart and serve Him alone above all else
Thou shalt not worship false gods or spiritual powers other than the Lord
Thou shalt have no graven images or likenesses of anything in heaven or on earth
The first commandment is, "Thou shalt have no other Gods before me."
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: The first commandment is, "Thou shalt have no other Gods before me."

options: An all-powerful being bound by time and subject to change like creation.
A Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in His being, wisdom, power.
A finite deity with limitations in knowledge, power, or moral perfection.
A material being with a physical body in some location in space.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: A Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in His being, wisdom, power.

options: To demonstrate that human effort and obedience can achieve the righteousness required by God
To show God's hatred of sinners and to condemn unbelievers to eternal punishment
To reveal God's perfect righteousness so His people know His will and ungodly are convicted
To prepare people for salvation by removing sins through perfect obedience to God's commands
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: To reveal God's perfect righteousness so His people know His will and ungodly are convicted

options: Some sins, by reason of aggravations, are more heinous in God's sight
The severity of sin depends entirely on how we feel about it
Sins against men are more serious than sins against God
All sins are equally sinful and deserve the same punishment
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Some sins, by reason of aggravations, are more heinous in God's sight

options: A saving grace whereby we receive and rest upon Christ alone for salvation
Belief in Christian doctrine and intellectual agreement that Jesus died for human sins
Commitment to moral self-improvement and personal effort to live according to biblical principles
Trust in religious works and sacraments through the church for eternal life and salvation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: A saving grace whereby we receive and rest upon Christ alone for salvation

options: Established by church councils as tests of faith and loyalty to Christian authority
Commanded by God in the Old Testament as signs of judgment for sin
Created by church tradition to symbolize spiritual truths without conferring any real grace to believers
Specially instituted by Christ to represent and apply to believers benefits of the new covenant
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:keachs_c.answer_choice: Specially instituted by Christ to represent and apply to believers benefits of the new covenant

options: God's rule is written in nature and can be understood through reason alone
The Word of God in the Scriptures of Old and New Testaments is the only rule to glorify God
God has given multiple rules including Scripture, church tradition, and personal experience
The Ten Commandments alone are sufficient to direct us in glorifying God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:puritan_.answer_choice: The Word of God in the Scriptures of Old and New Testaments is the only rule to glorify God

options: Thou shalt not swear by God's name falsely or make rash oaths that thou intendest later to break
Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; the Lord will not hold him guiltless
Thou shalt keep all thy vows made unto the Lord and not speak profanely or irreverently of His holy name
Thou shalt always speak reverently of God and avoid all forms of profanity, blasphemy, and irreverent speech toward Him
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:puritan_.answer_choice: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; the Lord will not hold him guiltless

options: Infants should be baptized as members of Christian families in obedience to church tradition
No; infants are not to be baptized; there is neither command nor example in Scripture
Children must be baptized to receive saving grace, since baptism removes original sin
Yes, infants may be baptized because they inherit the covenant through believing parents
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:puritan_.answer_choice: No; infants are not to be baptized; there is neither command nor example in Scripture

options: They suggest believers should remember Christ's ascension until His work is completed
They refer to Christ's spiritual presence in the Supper and His continued fellowship
They indicate that the church will continue until all nations are evangelized
They teach that Jesus Christ will come a second time, which is the joy and hope of believers
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:puritan_.answer_choice: They teach that Jesus Christ will come a second time, which is the joy and hope of believers

lead_in.question: What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper?
lead_in.answer: It is required of them who would worthily partake of the Lord's Supper, that they examine themselves of their knowledge to discern the Lord's body, of their faith to feed upon him, of their repentance, love, and new obedience, lest coming unworthily, they eat and drink judgment to themselves.

options: The Father begets the Son, the Son is begotten of the Father, and the Holy Ghost proceeds from both eternally.
The Father is almighty and eternal, the Son is our Redeemer and mediator, and the Holy Spirit is our comforter and guide.
The Father made the heavens and earth, the Son became incarnate and died for our sins, and the Spirit sanctifies believers.
The Father is the source of all things, the Son reveals the Father's will, and the Spirit applies redemption to believers.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The Father begets the Son, the Son is begotten of the Father, and the Holy Ghost proceeds from both eternally.

options: Only the preface and reasons of the Ten Commandments require consideration, not their substance
The substance of the commandments is the only thing to consider; the preface and reasons are less important
Consider the preface, substance of the commandments, and reasons annexed to some to enforce them
The commandments have no particular preface or annexed reasons, but stand as bare commands from God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Consider the preface, substance of the commandments, and reasons annexed to some to enforce them

options: The sum of our duty to God is to perfectly obey the Ten Commandments and keep all his statutes
To fear God's wrath, obey his law, and trust only in his provision for our lives
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind
To love God with all our might and to perform all the works that demonstrate this love
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, strength, and mind

options: Disrespect to parents, false oaths, evil thoughts about neighbors, and failure to keep the Sabbath.
False worship, witchcraft, neglect of prayer, self-righteousness, and lying about one's faith to others.
Covetousness, theft, murder, and adultery, which violate the commands about love of neighbor.
Atheism, idolatry, omission of duties, ignorance, false thoughts of God, profaneness, hatred, self-love, inordinate affections, unbelief, despair, hardness, pride, tempting God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Atheism, idolatry, omission of duties, ignorance, false thoughts of God, profaneness, hatred, self-love, inordinate affections, unbelief, despair, hardness, pride, tempting God

options: They possess some divine attributes like wisdom and power but not full equality with the Father.
Scripture shows the Son and Spirit are God equal with the Father by ascribing to them God's proper names and attributes.
They are called god-like beings but are subordinate to the Father and derive their powers from Him.
The Bible distinguishes three different levels of divine being, with the Father supreme and the others lesser.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Scripture shows the Son and Spirit are God equal with the Father by ascribing to them God's proper names and attributes.

options: The sabbath is primarily for the common people; superiors need only ensure legal observance
Directed to governors and superiors; they must keep it and ensure those under them observe it and not hinder them
The sabbath command applies equally to all people without any special charge to superiors and governors
Governors and superiors are exempt from keeping the sabbath so they can oversee their responsibilities
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Directed to governors and superiors; they must keep it and ensure those under them observe it and not hinder them

options: Remembering the Sabbath means taking time for rest alone, without concern for spiritual worship or creation's significance
The word Remember is included to remind us that the Sabbath was created for human convenience and leisure
Remembering helps in preparation and keeping it, recalls creation and redemption, comes once weekly amid competing worldly cares and cares
The fourth commandment requires God's people to work six days with one day of rest in complete idleness
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Remembering helps in preparation and keeping it, recalls creation and redemption, comes once weekly amid competing worldly cares and cares

options: To rule over your neighbor wisely and ensure they fulfill their obligations to you
Love your neighbor as yourself, and do to others as you would have them do to you
