The sum of duty to man is to seek your own good first and help others when convenient
To maintain justice and equality by giving others what they earn through their own efforts
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Love your neighbor as yourself, and do to others as you would have them do to you

options: Spiritual leaders and pastors exclusively, since the church is God's institution for directing believers' lives and growth
Political rulers and civic authorities alone, who govern the commonwealth and deserve honor as representatives of God
Not only natural parents, but all superiors in age and gifts, especially those in authority in family, church, commonwealth
Only biological parents, since the commandment specifically uses the word 'father' and 'mother' literally in each case
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Not only natural parents, but all superiors in age and gifts, especially those in authority in family, church, commonwealth

options: Styled Father and Mother to teach superiors to be like parents expressing love and tenderness, making inferiors more willing in duties
Styled Father and Mother merely as traditional honorary titles honoring ancient custom, without implying loving care or concern
Called Father and Mother to reflect their absolute authority and power, similar to how strict parents govern children
Named Father and Mother because superiors must exercise firm discipline and correction over inferiors, like fathers discipline children
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Styled Father and Mother to teach superiors to be like parents expressing love and tenderness, making inferiors more willing in duties

options: Obedience to their commands, loving affection toward them as parents, and protection from all public criticism.
Respect shown outwardly, submission to their lawful authority, and honor to their position without question.
Prayer for their guidance, eager compliance with their every desire, and defense of their actions blindly.
Superiors are styled Father and Mother to teach them duty toward inferiors, express love and tenderness, and make inferiors more willing to obey.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Superiors are styled Father and Mother to teach them duty toward inferiors, express love and tenderness, and make inferiors more willing to obey.

lead_in.question: What is the general scope of the fifth commandment?
lead_in.answer: The general scope of the fifth commandment is, the performance of those duties which we mutually owe in our several relations, as inferiors, superiors, or equals.

also_right: Respect shown outwardly, submission to their lawful authority, and honor to their position without question.

options: Failing to honor them, breaking their rules, showing anger and resentment, and speaking against them to others.
Disobedience to their commands, speaking disrespectfully and critically, refusing their correction, and showing contempt for them.
Unwillingness to obey, private criticism of them, and doubt of their authority, wisdom, and competence.
Inferiors owe superiors reverence, prayer, imitation of virtues, willing obedience, submission to correction, and defense of their authority in love.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Inferiors owe superiors reverence, prayer, imitation of virtues, willing obedience, submission to correction, and defense of their authority in love.

lead_in.question: What is the honor that inferiors owe to their superiors?
lead_in.answer: The honor which inferiors owe to their superiors is, all due reverence in heart, word, and behavior; prayer and thanksgiving for them; imitation of their virtues and graces; willing obedience to their lawful commands and counsels; due submission to their corrections; fidelity to, defense and maintenance of their persons and authority, according to their several ranks, and the nature of their places; bearing with their infirmities, and covering them in love, that so they may be an honor to them and to their government.

also_right: Disobedience to their commands, speaking disrespectfully and critically, refusing their correction, and showing contempt for them.

options: To rule with strict authority, maintain distance, and require absolute obedience without mercy or consideration.
Love, pray for, and instruct inferiors; reward the good, chasten the evil, provide for needs, and set holy examples.
To be friends with inferiors, share all authority equally, and let them do as they wish.
To demand perfection from inferiors and dismiss them harshly when they fail or make mistakes.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Love, pray for, and instruct inferiors; reward the good, chasten the evil, provide for needs, and set holy examples.

lead_in.question: What are the sins of inferiors against their superiors?
lead_in.answer: The sins of inferiors against their superiors are, all neglect of the duties required toward them; envying at, contempt of, and rebellion against, their persons and places, in their lawful counsels, commands, and corrections; cursing, mocking, and all such refractory and scandalous carriage, as proves a shame and dishonor to them and their government.

options: God elected all people to salvation through Christ and earnestly desires that none should perish but all be saved.
God has eternally elected some angels to glory and some men to eternal life in Christ, and foreordained others to wrath.
God chose some to be His covenant people based on His foreknowledge of their goodness and righteousness.
God foresaw who would believe in Christ and predestined only those who exercise faith to salvation and eternal life.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God has eternally elected some angels to glory and some men to eternal life in Christ, and foreordained others to wrath.

options: Attempting to reform subordinates' personal character beyond their calling and role, extending authority improperly into family and personal private affairs
Neglect of duties, seeking own glory and pleasure, commanding unlawful things, counseling in evil, dissuading from good, unduly correcting, exposing to danger
Overexercising power and authority beyond lawful limits, denying subordinates any freedom of personal conscience, and demanding their complete obedience
Any failure whatsoever to enforce established laws and rules, showing unwarranted mercy when discipline is deserved, and refusing to correct subordinates
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Neglect of duties, seeking own glory and pleasure, commanding unlawful things, counseling in evil, dissuading from good, unduly correcting, exposing to danger

options: Regard each other's dignity and worth, give honor, and rejoice in each other's gifts and advancement
To subordinate yourself to whichever equal seems most worthy at any given time
To maintain strict equality by never allowing anyone to receive greater honor or advancement
To compete with one another for recognition and to advance your own gifts above others
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Regard each other's dignity and worth, give honor, and rejoice in each other's gifts and advancement

options: Honoring one person more than others, preferring certain friendships above other relationships within the community
Celebrating others' success, acknowledging their talents, and supporting their advancement in various areas of life
Respecting authority figures and accepting their leadership role within the church and social structure
Neglect of duties, undervaluing worth, envying gifts, grieving at advancement and prosperity, usurping preeminence
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Neglect of duties, undervaluing worth, envying gifts, grieving at advancement and prosperity, usurping preeminence

options: Taking life is completely forbidden in all circumstances whatsoever, including lawful public justice, defensive warfare, and self-defense against attackers
Killing is prohibited except when motivated by personal anger and revenge, and when defending one's own honor and reputation
Murder is forbidden, but sinful anger toward wrongdoers, quarreling with rivals, harsh words, and striking in self-defense are permitted
Taking life except public justice, war, or defense; sinful anger, hatred, envy, revenge; immoderate use; provoking words; oppression; quarreling; striking
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Taking life except public justice, war, or defense; sinful anger, hatred, envy, revenge; immoderate use; provoking words; oppression; quarreling; striking

options: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.
The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not bear false witness.
The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt honor thy father and mother.
The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not commit adultery.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.

options: From the sinner's knowledge, position, and power; offense against superiors; and public commission
From breaking express law, offense against the innocent, violation of sacred time, and malice
From the sinner's deliberate intent and resistance to correction, scandal caused, and persistence
From the persons offending, parties offended, nature of offense, and circumstances of time and place
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: From the persons offending, parties offended, nature of offense, and circumstances of time and place

lead_in.question: Are all transgressions of the law of God equally heinous in themselves, and in the sight of God?
lead_in.answer: All transgressions of the law of God are not equally heinous; but some sins in themselves, and by reason of several aggravations, are more heinous in the sight of God than others.

options: Not all permitted to read publicly; all bound to read privately with families; scriptures translated to vulgar languages
All people are permitted and encouraged to read God's word publicly in the congregation without restriction
Only trained ministers and church leaders should read Scripture, not common people in their homes
The word should remain only in original languages so people depend on authorized interpreters
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Not all permitted to read publicly; all bound to read privately with families; scriptures translated to vulgar languages

options: With reverent esteem, firm persuasion they are God's word, desire to obey, diligence, attention, meditation, application, self-denial, and prayer
Quickly skimming Scripture to find isolated verses supporting one's existing beliefs and opinions without careful study
By casual reading without much reflection, accepting church teachings as equally authoritative as the biblical text itself
Privately reading Scripture while skeptical of its authority, trusting personal interpretation over scholarly and church tradition
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: With reverent esteem, firm persuasion they are God's word, desire to obey, diligence, attention, meditation, application, self-denial, and prayer

options: Any believer with zeal for God may preach the word publicly without formal approval
The word should be preached by all who have good intentions and moral character
Preaching requires only approval from the local congregation, not genuine spiritual gifts
Only by those sufficiently gifted, duly approved, and called to the office of preaching
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Only by those sufficiently gifted, duly approved, and called to the office of preaching

options: Whatever convicts the conscience and moves the heart, even if not clearly supported by Scripture.
Smooth and appealing words using human wisdom, suited to the hearers' preferences and understanding.
Doctrines adapted to the listeners' beliefs and expectations, avoiding those that trouble or offend.
Sound doctrine, plainly, faithfully the whole counsel, wisely, zealously, sincerely, with Spirit's demonstration
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Sound doctrine, plainly, faithfully the whole counsel, wisely, zealously, sincerely, with Spirit's demonstration

options: God created angels as immortal, holy spirits of knowledge and power, to execute commandments and praise God, yet subject to change.
God fashioned the angels from the dust of the earth as He did man, but gave them spiritual bodies.
God caused the angels to evolve from lower creatures over time, perfecting them into spiritual beings of great power.
God created angels as pure spirits composed of divine substance, eternal and unchangeable like God Himself.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God created angels as immortal, holy spirits of knowledge and power, to execute commandments and praise God, yet subject to change.

options: Sacraments administered automatically convey grace to anyone who participates, regardless of faith or covenant status
A sacrament is a human institution designed to teach morality and good behavior
A sacrament is merely a symbolic ritual without true spiritual significance or connection to Christ's mediation
Holy ordinance instituted by Christ to signify, seal, and exhibit benefits of his mediation to those in covenant of grace
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Holy ordinance instituted by Christ to signify, seal, and exhibit benefits of his mediation to those in covenant of grace

options: The inward grace is what matters; the outward sign is arbitrary and could be changed
The parts of sacraments vary; some have only outward signs and others only inward grace
Only the outward sign matters in a sacrament; the spiritual grace is entirely dependent on the recipient's faith
Two parts: an outward sensible sign according to Christ's appointment, and an inward spiritual grace signified thereby
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Two parts: an outward sensible sign according to Christ's appointment, and an inward spiritual grace signified thereby

options: Frequent re-baptism as a sign of renewed commitment and deepening faith in Christ and His covenant.
Serious and thankful consideration of baptism's nature, benefits, and vow; humbling for sin; assurance of pardon; drawing strength from Christ's death
Remembrance of baptism in prayer and thanksgiving, trusting in the sacrament's power to preserve faith.
Increasing strength in fighting sin through personal moral effort and determined will to obey God's law.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Serious and thankful consideration of baptism's nature, benefits, and vow; humbling for sin; assurance of pardon; drawing strength from Christ's death

options: Ministers set apart bread and wine by word of institution, thanksgiving, and prayer; give to communicants who eat and drink
The priest consecrates bread and wine, magically changing their substance into Christ's body and blood
Bread and wine remain only symbols with no special treatment, distributed like ordinary food to church members
The blessing transforms elements into Christ's literal body through the power of consecration formula
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Ministers set apart bread and wine by word of institution, thanksgiving, and prayer; give to communicants who eat and drink

options: Symbolically in remembrance, mentally receiving Christ by memory and understanding, not truly his substance
Corporally and literally, since through consecration the bread becomes Christ's actual body and blood
Sacramentally, the elements containing and conveying Christ's presence instrumentally through the church's ministry
Spiritually, not carnally, present to faith; truly and really receiving Christ crucified and his benefits
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Spiritually, not carnally, present to faith; truly and really receiving Christ crucified and his benefits

options: Examine only their doctrinal knowledge, moral behavior, and determination to avoid future sins
Examine their being in Christ, faith, sins, love to God and brethren, forgiveness; renew by prayer
Trust in God's grace alone, examine no private condition, make confession to the church
Fast from food, confess their sins to a priest, perform set penances beforehand
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Examine their being in Christ, faith, sins, love to God and brethren, forgiveness; renew by prayer

options: Those unsure of faith should wait until achieving perfect certainty of belief before approaching the communion table
Anyone doubting their salvation is automatically unfit for communion and should be refused the sacrament by church leaders
People uncertain of their conversion should abstain from communion until achieving complete and perfect certainty of grace
May have true interest if affected by lack and unfeignedly desires Christ; sacrament for weak and doubting; should come for strengthening
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: May have true interest if affected by lack and unfeignedly desires Christ; sacrament for weak and doubting; should come for strengthening

options: No; Christ commands all believers to come, and none should ever be excluded
Yes; the ignorant and scandalous are to be excluded by church power until reformed
Yes; by the magistrate and civil government, based on proof of moral worthiness
Yes; only those who deny the faith openly; those struggling may still approach
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Yes; the ignorant and scandalous are to be excluded by church power until reformed

options: Quietly and reverently, watch the minister's actions, observe the bread and wine, listen carefully
Carefully observe the consecration, discern whether the substance has changed, examine personal unworthiness
Eat and drink with dignity and silence, recall sufferings, examine personal moral state
With reverence and attention, discern the Lord's body, meditate on death, judge themselves, feed by faith
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: With reverence and attention, discern the Lord's body, meditate on death, judge themselves, feed by faith

options: Reflect on their behavior; if blessed, bless God and attend frequently; if not, review and improve
Thank God always for grace received, live confidently going forward, examine less frequently after
Trust that grace was received, make public profession of faith, need not attend frequently again
Examine whether they felt grace, determine fitness to approach again, do penance if lacking benefit
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Reflect on their behavior; if blessed, bless God and attend frequently; if not, review and improve

options: Both authored by God; spiritual part is Christ and his benefits; seals of same covenant; dispensed by gospel ministers only
Both sacraments are optional ceremonies that may be dispensed by any faithful believer
Baptism and the Supper are different in their authors, spiritual meanings, and how they should be administered
The sacraments were instituted by the apostles as Church traditions and will end with the current age
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Both authored by God; spiritual part is Christ and his benefits; seals of same covenant; dispensed by gospel ministers only

options: Baptism administered once with water for regeneration; Lord's supper administered often with bread and wine for spiritual nourishment
Both baptism and Lord's supper administered once with water and bread as signs and seals of faith
Baptism administered often with water for regeneration; Lord's supper administered once with bread and wine for nourishment
Baptism with bread and wine for regeneration; Lord's supper with water for spiritual nourishment of believers
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Baptism administered once with water for regeneration; Lord's supper administered often with bread and wine for spiritual nourishment

options: Saints and angels hear requests and pardon sins; prayer may be made to them for intercession
God, magistrates, and ministers can hear prayer; prayer is to be made to all of them
God only can search hearts, hear requests, and pardon sins; prayer is to be made to him alone
God and deceased saints hear prayer; they should be prayed to for their intercession with God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God only can search hearts, hear requests, and pardon sins; prayer is to be made to him alone

options: Pray using Christ's own words and methods, obey his commands exactly, repeat his formulas
Merely invoke his name at beginning and end, summoning his power to grant petitions
Ask God to grant desires because Christ earned merits, using his name as authority
In confidence on his promises, ask mercy for his sake, drawing boldness from Christ's mediation
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: In confidence on his promises, ask mercy for his sake, drawing boldness from Christ's mediation

options: The Old Testament law required it; covenant promises depend on using Christ's name in all our prayers
Man's sinfulness and distance from God make Christ alone the appointed mediator; we must pray in his name
The Spirit commands it in Scripture; apostles taught it as the primary way to approach God in prayer
Mary, the mother of Jesus, intercedes for us as the great mediator between God and all sinners
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Man's sinfulness and distance from God make Christ alone the appointed mediator; we must pray in his name

options: Spirit teaches only the elect and learned how to pray; common people must rely on ministers
Spirit helps by enabling understanding of for whom, what, and how to pray; works requisite graces in our hearts
Spirit prevents sinful thoughts and makes prayer unnecessary through constant intervention; helps only the ordained clergy pray
Spirit writes down prayers and presents them to God; only ministers' prayers receive God's full attention
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Spirit helps by enabling understanding of for whom, what, and how to pray; works requisite graces in our hearts

options: Ourselves and our friends only; prayers for others are presumptuous and beyond our proper Christian concern
Magistrates and ministers only, as they are appointed by God to receive our petitions and prayers
Whole church, magistrates, ministers, ourselves, brethren, enemies, and all men living or to come; but not the dead
All men, living, dead, and yet to be born, including those who have sinned the sin unto death
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Whole church, magistrates, ministers, ourselves, brethren, enemies, and all men living or to come; but not the dead

options: All things tending to God's glory, the church's welfare, our own or others' good; but not unlawful things
Only spiritual blessings and matters of soul; material needs and worldly prosperity are not proper prayer requests
God's glory alone, never our own welfare or others', as such prayer would be selfish and wrong
Anything we desire and request, whether lawful or unlawful, as God judges all petitions impartially
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: All things tending to God's glory, the church's welfare, our own or others' good; but not unlawful things

options: With boldness and familiarity, presuming confidently on God's mercy and approaching the throne as equals.
With assurance of always being heard and answered, and confidence that God agrees with our desires.
With requests focused only on spiritual blessings, avoiding earthly concerns and material needs in prayer.
With apprehension of God's majesty, sense of unworthiness, penitent and thankful hearts, understanding, faith, sincerity, fervency, love, and perseverance
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: With apprehension of God's majesty, sense of unworthiness, penitent and thankful hearts, understanding, faith, sincerity, fervency, love, and perseverance

options: Primarily as an expression of Christian identity, more important for memorization than for actual prayer practice
Only as a pattern to learn from, never to be used directly as a prayer in worship services
As a magical formula believed to guarantee answered prayers when recited with sufficient emotional intensity and frequency
As pattern for other prayers and as prayer itself, with understanding, faith, reverence, and other necessary graces
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: As pattern for other prayers and as prayer itself, with understanding, faith, reverence, and other necessary graces

options: Four parts: preface, petitions, doxology, and conclusion
Three parts: a preface, petitions, and a conclusion
Seven parts distributed throughout the prayer in theological order
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Three parts: a preface, petitions, and a conclusion

options: God permitted all angels to fall willfully into sin and damnation; He employs them to bring glory to Satan.
God permitted some angels to fall willfully into sin and damnation; He established the rest in holiness and employs both to His glory.
God prevented some angels from falling into sin and damnation; the rest fell and are employed in judgment.
God permitted some angels to fall through temptation and weakness; He established the rest but employs some unwillingly.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God permitted some angels to fall willfully into sin and damnation; He established the rest in holiness and employs both to His glory.

options: As a consequence of living in their sinful world and inheriting the corruption they caused.
Original sin passes from our first parents through natural generation to all their descendants conceived and born in sin.
Only to those who consciously imitate their disobedience and reject God's covenant as they did.
Through the example and influence of the sinful lifestyle that they established and taught their children.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Original sin passes from our first parents through natural generation to all their descendants conceived and born in sin.

lead_in.question: Wherein consists the sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell?
lead_in.answer: The sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell, consisteth in the guilt of Adam's first sin, the want of that righteousness wherein he was created, and the corruption of his nature, whereby he is utterly indisposed, disabled, and made opposite unto all that is spiritually good, and wholly inclined to all evil, and that continually; which is commonly called Original Sin, and from which do proceed all actual transgressions.

options: Physical sufferings, disease, poverty, loss of loved ones, and shortness of life approaching death.
Inward: blindness of mind, hardness of heart, horror of conscience. Outward: God's curse on creation and our evils in body and death.
Separation from family and community in this life, though with inner peace from knowing God.
Spiritual blindness and deepening despair in the soul, until physical death comes as relief.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Inward: blindness of mind, hardness of heart, horror of conscience. Outward: God's curse on creation and our evils in body and death.

lead_in.question: What misery did the fall bring upon mankind?
lead_in.answer: The fall brought upon mankind the loss of communion with God, his displeasure and curse; so as we are by nature children of wrath, bond slaves to Satan, and justly liable to all punishments in this world, and that which is to come.

options: Separation from God's presence without active torment, in darkness and silence but without positive pain.
Temporary punishment followed by restoration and eventual reconciliation with God after suffering is satisfied.
Everlasting separation from God's comfortable presence and most grievous torments in soul and body, without intermission, in hell fire forever.
Eternal sleep and unconsciousness as the soul's annihilation, ceasing to exist after physical death.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Everlasting separation from God's comfortable presence and most grievous torments in soul and body, without intermission, in hell fire forever.

options: The covenant of grace was made with Abraham and his descendants; it was renewed with the people of Israel.
The covenant of grace was made with Christ as the second Adam, and in him with all the elect as his seed.
The covenant of grace was made with all believers who trust in Jesus Christ as their personal Savior.
The covenant of grace was made with all humanity; God offers salvation freely to anyone who will accept it.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The covenant of grace was made with Christ as the second Adam, and in him with all the elect as his seed.

options: God gives His Holy Spirit only to those who work righteousness and demonstrate faith through good deeds.
God provides a Mediator; believers must work to receive faith through their own efforts and holy obedience.
God freely provides salvation through promises; believers must receive faith and achieve holiness through moral discipline.
God freely provides a Mediator and life and salvation by Him; He gives His Holy Spirit to work faith in believers and enable holy obedience.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God freely provides a Mediator and life and salvation by Him; He gives His Holy Spirit to work faith in believers and enable holy obedience.

options: The covenant of grace was not always administered the same way; Old Testament administrations differed from New Testament administrations.
There was one unified administration from Abraham onward, though Christ brought fuller revelation and truth.
The covenant itself changed; the administration remained the same throughout the Old and New Testaments.
The substance changed though the outward signs and sacraments remained similar in their basic form.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The covenant of grace was not always administered the same way; Old Testament administrations differed from New Testament administrations.

options: By promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, passover, and types which foresignified Christ to come; sufficient to give full remission of sins and eternal salvation.
By the moral law and keeping God's commandments perfectly, which would secure their righteousness and salvation.
Through sacrifices only, which never truly provided actual forgiveness but only covered sin temporarily.
By types and figures as shadows, but no actual grace was given until Christ's coming.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: By promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, passover, and types which foresignified Christ to come; sufficient to give full remission of sins and eternal salvation.

options: Primarily through the internal testimony of the Holy Spirit in the believer's heart and conscience.
Through preaching alone; the sacraments are merely memorial signs without real efficacy or grace.
By the sacraments only, with preaching as secondary support for the grace they convey.
By preaching the Word and administering Baptism and Lord's Supper; grace and salvation are held forth in fuller evidence and efficacy to all nations.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: By preaching the Word and administering Baptism and Lord's Supper; grace and salvation are held forth in fuller evidence and efficacy to all nations.

options: The church and its ordained ministers, who stand as mediators between God and individual believers in hearing confessions.
Moses and the prophets, through whom God mediated His covenant to the Old Testament people of Israel.
The Holy Spirit, who applies the grace of Christ to believers and mediates between God and the church through spiritual gifts.
The Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Son of God, equal with the Father, is the sole Mediator of the covenant of grace.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Son of God, equal with the Father, is the sole Mediator of the covenant of grace.

options: Divine nature was needed only to enable Him to rise from death and overcome Satan.
A god-like being possessing great divine power would suffice to satisfy God's justice adequately.
To prevent His human nature from being overwhelmed or destroyed by the infinite power of God.
God's Mediator must be God to sustain human nature under wrath, give worth to His sacrifice, satisfy justice, and bring salvation.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: God's Mediator must be God to sustain human nature under wrath, give worth to His sacrifice, satisfy justice, and bring salvation.

lead_in.question: How did Christ, being the Son of God, become man?
lead_in.answer: Christ the Son of God became man, by taking to himself a true body, and a reasonable soul, being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of the virgin Mary, of her substance, and born of her, yet without sin.

options: The Mediator must be man to obey the law, suffer and intercede for us, and give us access to God's grace.
His human nature enables Him to be tempted in all ways as we are tempted.
Human nature was needed to make Him relatable and sympathetic to human weakness and struggle.
Only as a man could He teach the true way of righteousness to His followers.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The Mediator must be man to obey the law, suffer and intercede for us, and give us access to God's grace.

lead_in.question: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be God?
lead_in.answer: It was requisite that the Mediator should be God, that he might sustain and keep the human nature from sinking under the infinite wrath of God, and the power of death; give worth and efficacy to his sufferings, obedience, and intercession; and to satisfy God's justice, procure his favor, purchase a peculiar people, give his Spirit to them, conquer all their enemies, and bring them to everlasting salvation.

options: To show that God and man are essentially the same and equal in nature.
So the human part could achieve perfection and the divine part ensure complete righteousness.
The Mediator must be God and man in one person so His divine and human works are accepted by God for us.
So He could be honored by both God and humans, being part of both groups.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The Mediator must be God and man in one person so His divine and human works are accepted by God for us.

lead_in.question: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be man?
lead_in.answer: It was requisite that the Mediator should be man, that he might advance our nature, perform obedience to the law, suffer and make intercession for us in our nature, have a fellow feeling of our infirmities; that we might receive the adoption of sons, and have comfort and access with boldness unto the throne of grace.

options: Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he is our Lord and King who rules over all nations.
Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he taught His disciples the way to eternal life and righteousness.
Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he saveth his people from their sins.
Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he heals the sick and performs mighty works and miracles.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he saveth his people from their sins.

options: His exalted state wherein Christ is advanced to the highest favor with God, possessing all power and glory in heaven and earth.
His miracles and mighty works by which He demonstrated His divine power and authority over sickness, demons, and nature.
That low condition wherein Christ, emptying Himself of glory, took the form of a servant from conception through death until resurrection.
His role as prophet, priest, and king, in which He teaches God's will, offers Himself as sacrifice, and rules creation.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: That low condition wherein Christ, emptying Himself of glory, took the form of a servant from conception through death until resurrection.

options: From eternity the Son of God in Father's bosom, He became son of man, made of a woman of low estate, born in abasement.
Born miraculously without human father; He was recognized by kings and shepherds as the great King of Israel.
Born to Mary, a righteous and faithful woman; He was blessed above all births and honored by all who saw Him.
Born during Caesar Augustus' reign; His birth brought great joy to Jerusalem and was welcomed by the Jewish leaders.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: From eternity the Son of God in Father's bosom, He became son of man, made of a woman of low estate, born in abasement.

options: By fulfilling only the ceremonial law; by enduring worldly suffering, demonic opposition, and natural human limitations.
By exempting Himself from the law's requirements and displaying divine power; by conquering worldly indignities without temptation.
By subjecting Himself to the law and perfectly fulfilling it; by conflicting with the world's indignities, Satan's temptations, and human infirmities.
By demonstrating perfect obedience to tradition and society; by avoiding Satan's temptations and remaining separate from human weakness.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: By subjecting Himself to the law and perfectly fulfilling it; by conflicting with the world's indignities, Satan's temptations, and human infirmities.

options: Betrayed, forsaken, rejected, condemned; He endured wrath, terrors of death and darkness, laid down His life as offering for sin on shameful cursed cross.
He suffered great physical pain and shame, yet remained spiritually exalted and comforted by the Father.
He endured Roman torture and humiliation, but was sustained and comforted by God's constant presence.
He experienced rejection and cruelty from men, but conquered death inwardly and spiritually through His Spirit.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Betrayed, forsaken, rejected, condemned; He endured wrath, terrors of death and darkness, laid down His life as offering for sin on shameful cursed cross.

options: Christ was buried by His disciples and remained in Hades until God raised Him on the third day.
Christ's body was laid in a tomb and His soul went to paradise; He was not truly dead but sleeping.
Christ was buried and remained under death's power for three days; expressed as 'He descended into hell.'
Christ's humiliation ended at death; after death He entered glory and ceased to suffer for mankind.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Christ was buried and remained under death's power for three days; expressed as 'He descended into hell.'

options: He appeared spiritually to the disciples but His actual body remained in the tomb eternally.
He took a new glorified body unlike the one that suffered and died on the cross.
He rose with His same body without corruption; He declared Himself God's Son, satisfied divine justice, vanquished death, and became Head of His Church.
He rose to vindication but remained subordinate to the Father's authority in the heavens.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: He rose with His same body without corruption; He declared Himself God's Son, satisfied divine justice, vanquished death, and became Head of His Church.

options: After forty days appearing and commissioning apostles to preach, He visibly ascended to highest heavens as our head, triumphing to prepare a place for us.
He went to heaven to await the final resurrection of the dead and end of the world.
He ascended to continue His mediatorial work in heaven entirely, separated from His earthly people.
He ascended spiritually but remained present on earth through His Spirit dwelling in believers.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: After forty days appearing and commissioning apostles to preach, He visibly ascended to highest heavens as our head, triumphing to prepare a place for us.

options: Christ rules only over the invisible church in heaven, having no authority or involvement with earthly matters and governments.
Christ waits passively in heaven until the day of judgment, performing no active work on behalf of His people.
Christ at God's right hand has full power and glory, defends His church, furnishes gifts and graces, and intercedes for us.
Christ continues in His humiliation, hiding His glory and submitting to the rule of earthly powers and Satan.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Christ at God's right hand has full power and glory, defends His church, furnishes gifts and graces, and intercedes for us.

options: By appearing before Father in our nature, presenting His merit and sacrifice, declaring their application to believers, answering accusations before God's throne.
By praying earnestly to the Father on behalf of believers for protection and spiritual blessings.
By sending the Holy Spirit to plead believers' case and intercede for them before God.
By making our works acceptable before the Father's judgment and presenting our merits to God.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: By appearing before Father in our nature, presenting His merit and sacrifice, declaring their application to believers, answering accusations before God's throne.

options: Christ shall return only in the hearts of believers through the work of the Holy Spirit, not in bodily form.
Christ shall come in humility and meekness, not in power and glory, to call all people to repentance and faith.
Christ shall come secretly and invisibly to rapture His church away before the world's destruction and final judgment.
Christ shall come at the last day in great power and glory, with His holy angels, to judge the world in righteousness.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Christ shall come at the last day in great power and glory, with His holy angels, to judge the world in righteousness.

options: Christ by His obedience procured righteousness for believers; His sacrifice removed all punishment from those who trust in Him.
Christ by His death procured forgiveness for believers; His resurrection ensures that all will eventually reach heaven.
Christ by His teaching procured wisdom for believers; His example shows us the way to eternal life and happiness.
Christ, by his mediation, hath procured redemption, with all other benefits of the covenant of grace.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Christ, by his mediation, hath procured redemption, with all other benefits of the covenant of grace.

options: Those who faithfully keep the moral law, produce good works, and demonstrate their worthiness through righteous living.
All people universally, since Christ's redemption is offered to all and none are excluded from the possibility of salvation.

options: The scriptures make known what God requires of us, how He forgave all sins, and how we should live.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The scriptures make known what God is, the persons in the Godhead, his decrees, and the execution of his decrees.

options: No, but God ensures that all people eventually hear the gospel message before they die.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Those without the gospel cannot be saved, even through moral effort. Salvation is only in Christ, the Savior of His church.

lead_in.question: Who are made partakers of redemption through Christ?
lead_in.answer: Redemption is certainly applied, and effectually communicated, to all those for whom Christ hath purchased it; who are in time by the Holy Ghost enabled to believe in Christ according to the gospel.

options: Yes. All baptized members of the visible church and their children are certainly saved by its grace.

No. Many are saved outside the visible church through other religions and sincere moral living.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: Not all who hear the gospel and live in the visible church are saved, but only true members of the invisible church.

lead_in.question: Can they who have never heard the gospel, and so know not Jesus Christ, nor believe in him, be saved by their living according to the light of nature?
lead_in.answer: They who, having never heard the gospel, know not Jesus Christ, and believe not in him, cannot be saved, be they never so diligent to frame their lives according to the light of nature, or the laws of that religion which they profess; neither is there salvation in any other, but in Christ alone, who is the Savior only of his body the church.

options: Authority to forgive sins on God's behalf, power to mediate salvation, and governance over conscience.
The visible church enjoys God's special care, protection, and preservation; communion of saints, means of salvation, and gospel offers excluding none who will come.
Certainty of salvation for all members, special revelations from heaven, and direct divine guidance.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The visible church enjoys God's special care, protection, and preservation; communion of saints, means of salvation, and gospel offers excluding none who will come.

options: The invisible church is the sum of all believers who have reached heaven; they continue to intercede for the living.
The invisible church is the whole number of the elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one under Christ the head.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: The invisible church is the whole number of the elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one under Christ the head.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: All the elect, and only they, are effectually called; others may be outwardly called but never truly come to Christ

options: They may hope and expect assurance but cannot have certainty without an extraordinary revelation from God.

lead_in.question: May not true believers, by reason of their imperfections, and the many temptations and sins they are overtaken with, fall away from the state of grace ?
lead_in.answer: True believers, by reason of the unchangeable love of God, and his decree and covenant to give them perseverance, their inseparable union with Christ, his continual intercession for them, and the Spirit and seed of God abiding in them, can neither totally nor finally fall away from the state of grace, but are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation.

options: Yes. All true believers always maintain full assurance of their salvation and never experience doubt.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.answer_choice: True believers may lack assurance long or lose it through temptations, but the Spirit prevents them from sinking into despair.

lead_in.question: Can true believers be infallibly assured that they are in the estate of grace, and that they shall persevere therein unto salvation?
lead_in.answer: Such as truly believe in Christ, and endeavor to walk in all good conscience before him, may, without extraordinary revelation, by faith grounded upon the truth of God's promises, and by the Spirit enabling them to discern in themselves those graces to which the promises of life are made, and bearing witness with their spirits that they are the children of God, be infallibly assured that they are in the estate of grace, and shall persevere therein unto salvation.
